comment: Beautiful bike! One large tree down at the beginning. No bugs!

Just short of 11km. Spectacular views, natural paths with varied terrain (smooth rock, jagged rock, roots, dirt, logs, etc.). Very well marked (yet discreet markings) to keep you on the right path. Trails brings you in and out of the forest, along the mountain ridge with amazing views, and along creeks and ponds. Great variety, good elevation gain, and a great workout. Not many steep descents so no need for poles for most people. Took our family of 4 (two kids - 15, 8) just under 4 hrs including a lunch break.

This trail was beautiful, there are guide books to grab at the start of trail which provide info on 13 different “posts” throughout the 10.4km route. We went in the summer but could imagine how beautiful it is in the fall with the foliage. There are some steep climbs that definitely get the heart pumping but are so worth it for all of the lookouts. Took us 4h 30mins including breaks for food and water. Bring bug spray, snacks and water.

One hell of a trail. Initially underestimated it a bit. Got some serious elevation at time. For the most part, totally doable and I would rate it moderate. The views are amazing up there and its worth the walk!
no bathrooms, lots of little frogs to keep an eye out for, saw a turtle

Beautiful trail through quiet, peaceful woods.  Probably came across 15 other people the entire hike.  Lots of stumps and rocks, need to keep an eye out.  Would have been much more difficult when wet.  The views are well worth a few steep climbs!  Parking lot was practically empty at 10, pretty full when we finished around 1:30.  Bugs are definitely more noticeable in the second half around the ponds and streams.

Beautiful hike! More strenuous than difficult. No special gear required. We managed in running shoes but recommend doing the hike in hiking boots. Applied bug spray before hitting the trail and were fine. Enjoy!
Very hard tail.

Best trail in Algonquin! Took us about 4 hours, we started at 655am sharp. Although the trail was long and the inclines were at times, tough, there are regular lookouts that made it beyond worth it! The history and signage along the trail added to the experience. Highly recommend going earlier in the day, and bringing bug repellent, and appropriate clothing. The ladder half of the trail was quite muddy and slippery, but this was early June after regular rain storms.
Visited on 19 July, there were almost no bugs. Ground slightly wet from the rain the day before
Wonderful views, nice trail

Stats aren’t accurate as my device kept connecting and disconnecting. If you are looking for an Ontario hike that gives that mountain feel, this one is it. Great heights, beautiful views and nice diversity between forest, ponds and massive slabs of the Canadian Shield. Saw lots of little frogs and chipmunks. Bugs were not bad at all, but the morning was cooler (11-14c). Big parking lot and outhouses at the trailhead.
Great Great views, mug spray is must. Try to have large bottle of water.
Perfect day on the trail. Almost no bugs! Fantastic views!
Bring your bug spray! Beautiful hike, some boggy spots but people have made little detours around them that are dry so didn’t get muddy. Lots of up and down and little frogs and pretty butterflies.

This is an excellent trail, may be a bit difficult for some people. We really enjoyed this trail, a perfect hike through the forest, up and down hills, with a bit of rocky terrain, and of course, beautiful views.
Lots of bugs at this time and muddy. Honestly the best view’s are at the end of the circles so no need to do middle part. Just go left to view and turn around, than far right, turn around :)
A lot of freaking bugs that taunt you
Multiple scenic lookouts throughout the trail with beautiful views! Hard but worth it!
Lots of muddy spots.  Well marked.  💜 this trail.    Moderate to hard   some steep hills. Many roots and rocks.   Gorgeous views.   The epitome of Algonquin PP.
Lots of ups and downs. Beautiful views all throughout, lots of wildlife.
Great hike. I ran some of it because I needed to get back before dark. But loved it. Lots of bugs and mud
There is a large parking lot by the trailhead, and the trail itself was not crowded at all when I went. There were lots of viewpoints along the trail, but also LOTS of mosquitoes.
A few muddy spots and downed trees otherwise the trail is in great condition. Great views as always!
Be sure to douse yourself in Bug Spray and they’ll leave you alone. One of my favouite trails in Algonquin. Never disappoints.

Beautiful trail, but the bugs are brutal right now! 🌲🦟
A very nice trail with excellent Canadian nature scenery. However, it wasn't totally enjoyable in June due to the heavy amount of mosquitoes and black flies, along with muddy paths and hot, humid weather.

Great hike and well marked. There were a lot of mosquitoes and black flies when we went especially near the water but even at the viewpoints too.

Last viewpoint is the best so if you want a great view but don’t want to do the whole 10k I’d recommend doing the trail backwards until you hit the viewpoint.

Lots of frogs so watch under your feet!
The view is worth every single step
Spirit filling!
Gorgeous views! Definitely buggy this time of year. Muddy in some sections and a great workout.
buggy buggy buggy
So many mosquitoes
Unreal views, a bit demanding for beginners but worth the effort. 9/10.

Great trail! Marked very well. I consider it to be moderate to hard.  Lots of biting bugs today.  Was muddy in spots but nothing too horrible.  Definitely pack 2L of water.  The last lookout spot looking over whitefish lake was the prize!

There were a few spots that were even muddier than usual here, but that's to be expected with the spring rains. You can get around most of it, but one area in particular is bad if you dip into the mud pits. Lookouts are as spectacular as ever.

Beautiful trail in the Algonquin Provincial Park. Lots of great panoramic lookouts. Very varied wildlife both in the air and on the ground. Occasionally muddy, but with the right shoes this was no problem. No wildflowers yet, though.
Beautiful views from multiple lookouts. Well marked trail.
Great trail closer to home, def will do again. Muddy in some parts but manageable
Difficult steep climb but worth the breath taking views.
Excellent views and many different biomes to explore! Prepare for a longer journey, with a quicker pace we managed to go start-to-finish in just over 4 hours (taking time to stop and enjoy the views)
Some muddy spots right now but the views are worth it
Well marked trail with beautiful views. Parking lot is now open, and bugs aren’t out yet 👍
My husband and I and our dog Sophie 🐕 we hiked the trail 👣 today! We just went to the lookout today views were beautiful as they always are!
Great trail with nice elevation gains and views. Trail wasn't too muddy, well maintained, and nicely marked. Will definitely be back once everything is more in bloom.
Beautiful hike, views are worth all the incline. We took breaks and it took us about 3 hours and 15 minutes to complete.

Awesome trail with stunning views! No one seems to know that you can park at the Raccoon Lake Entrance early in the season, so it was great! There was some mud on the trail as to be expected, but could easily get around it.

Great condition and visibility, trail very easy to follow, not too muddy.
No bears in sight, a lot of moose’s tracks, one snake and several woodpecker.
Gate still shut so add 2km each way to the route

Dryer than expected for this time of year! Amazing views! Great conditions! 
Saw a moose on the way back to Huntsville!

It was a little early in the season so I had to walk in from hwy 60 as the parking wasn’t open.  Beautiful day, great conditions overall.  There were some wet areas but I assume that’s seasonal.  I did lose the trail for about 1/2 km … going counterclockwise the markers can be hard to see.  Tough trail but views are worth it!

One bathroom at the beginning of the trail which is an outhouse, really stinky and probably can give you infections. Overall, the trail was very good. Visited on Nov 10 last year so the leaves were all gone, but the views were great and there was decent elevation providing some difficulty.
First snow!

The parking lot is big, but it easily gets full. There are no washrooms nearby. The trail is not clearly marked; the identifiers along the way are just basic colours. It does not indicate which number you are on along the trail. Yes, it is a loop, but that information would have helped a lot, especially for people with navigational issues. (The people I came with got lost and ended up hiking 20kms; they were bone-tired). 

We went early in the morning, and there were already a lot of people when we came back. The view was spectacular! It looked like a gigantic nature art painting; my jaw dropped. We wanted to see the view from the side (the best view), but there was a group of people who stayed there for quite some time and did not even move an inch. Not to be racist, but they also smelled bad. 

Overall, it was worth it!
Beautiful walk with fantastic scenery. Clearly signposted, easy to park
Awesome views

Trail was busy but not crowded, not a ton of parking space. 
Great views, would definitely recommend!
Busy trail
Such amazing trail
Prepare for elevation. Definitely a hike not just a trail
Incredible lookout spots, lovely lakes, limited wildlife, too many humans.
A stunning trail, very varied and not boring. Not easy, but not difficult either. However, you have to watch your step almost all the time: rocks and polished roots everywhere.

This trail is long if you aren’t used to 6 plus miles of walking but it’s beautiful and not technical. Hiking boots and poles can help. I’m a hiker and my husband is not. He was wiped at the end but also very pleased with himself. Amazing views. We stopped often and it took 5 hours.

This trail was not difficult at all, just long and rocky/rooty. I almost didn’t do this hike because it was listed as difficult and I would’ve been really mad if I hadn’t, because I’d classify it as Easy and there were absolutely beautiful views. Took me just over 3 hours.
Definitely not hard just technical at some points. Great hike with lots of great lookouts!

This trail is very rewarding but has lots of challenges. Lots of elevation changes and ups and downs over rocks and roots. The distance of the trail is around 10 kms and took us around 5 hours to complete. Overall this hike was very difficult and tiring but worth the climb to amazing views.
Amazing! Lots of beautiful spots

Great trail however you do need a permit and I don’t think they limit how many people buy it since the parking lot was overcrowded and cars were parked on the side of the road. If you make your own spot you WILL get a parking ticket. Other than that the trail was great and marked really well.
I really enjoyed this one. Not easy but manageable. Good amount of incline and decline. Lookout points were 10/10.
Beautiful trail. Views were stunning. I would rate this as a moderate hike (not hard).

Moderate to difficult for Ontario. Give yourself at least 5 hours, especially if the area has had recent rains. When I did it, was after a bit of a dry spell and so no real mud or slippery rocks to be worried about, but that is rare in Algonquin.  One of my favorite trails in Algonquin.
Great nice trail with a lot of views.
That's one amazing trail.. Very rewarding views for the climbs.. Won't call it hard but it is not easy.. Sturdy boots and strong knees recommended..
If you start the loop around mid afternoon, you can watch the sunset from post 11!
I saw the reviews calling this a hard hike, but I think it’s best described as moderate with numerous roots and rocks.  great views!
Hard but the views are incredible !

We did not encounter many hikers on our route so it made for a quite peaceful hike. There were plenty of viewpoints but the one at pillar #10 was the most beautiful (with the large lake).

Fantastic views all around the trail.

Nice Trail, great views. Parking might be limited but you can park down the road.

October 3rd, full autumn weather and 28C. Absolutely stunning!

We did this trail clockwise and we were descending on the way out which worked very well. The views were just out of this world! I suspect because of the time of the year, stellar weather and leaves changing colors, the trail was super busy so this is the down side. Nice fall colours to see

We're probably a couple of weeks out for peak colour thanks to the heat waves but the maples are really givin 'er right now. The middle lookout section in particular is spectacular at the moment. The rest of the trail is just OK. The spots that are usually muddy aren't right now, so that's a plus.

Beautiful trail with multiple view points. Love a good fall view point over a cliff :). Trail is moderate-difficult. Def harder if muddy conditions. Proper shoes are a must, and carry plenty snacks/water.

Fantastic views from multiple locations throughout the hike.
Overall the hike is a fairly constant moderately technical hike. If you look up for too long while walking you will trip over or kick a tree root or rock.
I love this kind of terrain in the Canadian Shield, but you do have to pay attention where you are stepping almost constantly.
The elevation gain is accurate, but it is also spread out over many ups and downs.

Great sunny day with dry trail conditions. Had lunch on one of the many superb bluff views!
If you do it clockwise, as recommended, the views get progressively more impressive and beautiful. Really wonderful loop.
Dry hard packed well travelled and well marked trail. The weather was pleasant perfect, not too warm, sunny, no bugs.
This our favorite Algonquin trail. It had a variety of terrain and some steep section. Many gorgeous views scattered throughout the route. The view at post 11 was our favorite.
Pretty clear signs all across the trail. Snake sighted at lake lookout

Such a fun hike! Definitely a bit challenging at parts, but never unmanageable as long as you've got solid footwear. Conditions were beautiful, and the trail is very well-maintained. Amazing views at the lookout markers!
Beautiful day with fantastic views. It’s a challenging hike. Make sure you’re in reasonable shape to be able to complete this hike.
Great trail! Solid challenge for an Ontario hike. Definitely need to wear proper hiking shoes and keep your head up for trail makers.

My husband and I and our dog  Sophie we hiked the trail  today! It is a very hard trail but the lookout spots are beautiful!

The Algonquin map says this is a 6 hour hike but we finished it in under 5 hours with a break for lunch and many stops to admire the views. A few bugs in one boggy area but overall basically bug-free today.
Definitely some inclines but the amazing views are worth it!
Good trail, pretty dry now
Tough hike, challenging terrain, spectacular views!  We loved it!
Very scenic hike! Challenging if youre a beginner hiker but its my best hike at algonquin park
Enjoyed the trailer and we saw a beaver in one of the ponds somewhere between markers 8 and 10.

We did the trail clockwise and traveled at 3 km per hour. We found our hiking poles very useful given the amount of rocks and roots. Gorgeous views and was cool to see so many Beaver dams as part of the trail.

This trail has many fantastic views! You reach the first in about .75 miles in. I’m not in the best shape and the elevation was a bit tough for me but the views were definitely worth it! I started the trail at 3:30pm and had the whole thing to myself including the lookouts, total time was about 4 hours with semi-frequent snack breaks, stops for pictures and to catch my breath. Lots of parking and LOTS of mosquitos

In typical Algonquin Park fashion the toughest stuff is at the beginning, the best views in both directions are near the start of the loop at the top of the climb. There’s also great scenery in the middle. Stopped for lunch and to take a lot of picture and did it in just over 4 hours.

One of my favourites at Algonquin for a day hike, absolutely beautiful views, feels rewarding with all the lookouts. The trail has great maintenance and I have never not enjoyed this hike. Would recommend to anyone in the area. Look out for the silver birch near the end!!
The trail was to hard for me as my knee's were sore, I would go backwards and stop at pole #11 and have a picnic and return the same way back.

Moderate trail with challenging portions - suitable for most hikers but not for those with mobility issues. Bring plenty of water and snacks - with breaks it will take you approximately 4 hours. Very well maintained and blazed. Some areas washed out but easy to spot next marker to stay on course. Download map ahead of time - minimal service.

Incredibly beautiful and interesting trail. Loved the breezy ridges and all the lush beaver ponds and bogs. Very dry conditions, so minimal bugs.
lowkey rolled my ankle on this. 5/10

An awesome hike with beautiful views overlooking some wonderful Algonquin wilderness.
Great hike with enough length and elevation to get a good workout.  Great views and very well marked.

I am a 68’year old male who is in decent walking shape but not a runner fyi- I have hiked this trail several times in years past and consider it as one of the best day hikes in the park for wonderful vistas and changing terrains. To get the full experience of the 6 mile hike I suggest you hike it clockwise in direction of the loop. Also look carefully at the prior weather and if it has been raining, consider waiting for dryer conditions. There are several steep ascent and decent sections which become quite slippery if there has been rain in recent days. The views from up on top of the ridges are spectacular and well worth the effort involved. On the lower sections one hikes in and out of beautiful forest sections interspersed with occasional beaver ponds. These sections can be a little buggy. This trail is aptly viewed as a moderate or challenging day hike. Start in the morning and take your time to enjoy an incredible hike. Count on having lunch up on top soaking in the beautiful views. P.S. the picture of the big rock “face” reminds me of a gentle giant. Also I forgot to restart my app at one point so I’m not sure about the accuracy of the mileage. It’s definitely at least a 6 mile hike.

Enjoyed this trail immensely. Spectacular views in spite of wildfire haze, lots of variation on the trail. Do it clockwise.

Great trail. This is one of my favourites. Not very buggy today since it wasn’t too hot and the trail was pretty dry. Views are incredible! Took me about 4 hours but stopped a lot for snacks and to admire the view,
Great views throughout the hike. This is a difficult and long hike. Very enjoyable!

Trailer is in good condition. The bugs were not terrible. For parking, if you are camping within the Algonquin provincial Park parking is included in your reservation fees. Fantastic view in the afternoon. Go right for a quick hike to the top, and left for the longer round trip route.
It hasn’t rained in about 6 days so conditions were really good-not much mud and bugs weren’t an issue. Great views and a diverse terrain.

Fun but challenging. Prepare to sweat and feel exhausted. Gorgeous views and lots of wild life!

Gorgeous views, super well marked. A bit muddy but nothing major! Amazing hike.
beautiful hike!!! lots of mosquitoes but it was alright. really nice to just sit by the cliffs and take a break

Trail was very muddy, highly reccomend  wearing hiking boots. Views were very nice. Took longer than the estimated time, we did it in about 4 hours. My watch had it around 10.5-11 KM.

Great views along the ridges, certain muddy sections with fallen trees could be slippery, overall great trail with moderate difficulty

Pretty muddy towards the end, to be expected though. Not too bad to navigate plenty of rocks and fallen branches to walk on. Great views and not too windy or hot!

If you want 1 trail that exposes you to all Algonquin has to offer, this is the one!  Everything from rocky ridge views to wooded areas, beaver ponds and lake vistas. It has some mucky spots but most have dryish bypasses.  If you bring a dog, you may have to carry it across a couple sections to keep its feet from getting too muddy. Gorgeous views and a fun hike overall. Insane amount of bugs at this time of the year especially away from the ridge. I’d wear a light long sleeve shirt and pants. Very muddy at some points, wear waterproof shoes or boots. Follow the blue marker and you won’t get lost.

Great trail with great views! Bring lots of water. The trail goes up and down so be ready to climb an incline right after tackling a descent. The trail is mostly free of obstructions and there are only a few muddy spots. Lots of black flies and mosquitoes so recommend a bug spray.

Bring enough water and food.  If you want a short version of this trail go to the right at the fork and climb up to see the last ridge of the trail.
Muddy, incredible views, must to do

Tip: if you aren’t an experienced hiker, my recommendation is to go straight to the most scenic viewpoint (look up the Centennial Ridges Park map with numbers; you will need to go the points # 11 and 10 and skip the whole loop; this will require effort but it’s way easier than going the full hike).
Parking lot is big, but make sure to purchase the HWY 60 reservation at Ontarioparks website (as long as it’s required for the date of your visit), print it out and come in the morning to secure your spot. Otherwise, you may need to park at the side road even if you have a reservation. 
The full loop trail was hard for us but totally worth it. Amazing nature along the way. It took 4.5-5 hours even though we had only one little break. Muddy at some places but manageable. Wear comfortable shoes!

I loved this trail.  If you don’t want to do the full 12k you can go up one side go back down to the fork then go up the other side.  I recommend doing the left side first as the views on the right are much nicer.  The parking lot was jammed packed but the trail didn’t feel crowded.  There are bathrooms available but they’re pretty gross.  There were some muddy spot but we managed to get around them.  Overall very happy to have done this hike.
Saw a woodpecker and a toad
Challenging trail, with views of the lake and forest. A little muddy in many portions. Takes longer time than expected for the 11 km, because of the roots and rocks
Muddy in spots. Morning fog on the lake nearby.
Took us longer than expected because we had to stop a hundred times to take photos of the breathtaking views on this trail.
A little bit muddy easy trail

This was definitely not the easiest hike I’ve done, but I am not in the best of shape. Great views make it all worth it, many view points throughout the trail but definitely prep for 4.5-5 hours. Went when it was raining so there was plenty of mud, recommend a walking stick to help with balance through slippery sections

Stunning hike! 
We went the opposite way around to everyone else as it was beginning to get crowded. Had no issues parking when we arrived around 10:30 but by the time we’d finished the queues were all the way down the entry road. 
Took us 3.5 hours with a couple of stops.
Amazing trail, probably the best I've done in my life in fall
It took about six hours with dogs, but lots of beautiful sites. Pack food and lots of water.

Gets very crowded after 12:00pm , we started at around 8:30 with an almost empty parking lot and came back after 5.5 hours to at least a kilometer long parking line. 

The trail is every bit as amazing as the photos show. There are 13 points to cover in all. Point 2-3 , 3-4 , 6-7 are really intense but with beautiful views at the end. Point 8 to 9 is really long fades in comparison to the other points. Be prepared to hike for at least 6 hours and a little longer if you plan to take lots of photographs. 

Definitely pick up the hiking guide available for free at the entrance (but don’t forget to return it). If it has rained earlier, be prepared to hike through mud. This lives us to every bit of the difficulty rating!

Perfect fall conditions, way better than the previous rainy weekend, lesson learned, avoid this trail if it rains the day prior or on the day of. This hike is best enjoyed on dry weather days be it summer or fall, unless you want to spend your day traversing through the muck that it becomes.

You will definitely need a hiking stick! The trees are beautiful, especially in the fall, but this is definitely not an easy trail. A few muddy areas so you will definitely need appropriate hiking boots! When you get to the top, the view is absolutely worth it.
Great vistas well worth it. Arrive before 10am or you are dealing either the insta crowd at the view points. Not a lot of mud - as long as you have waterproof shoes!
It

Trail was difficult very technical, lots of rocks and roots covered in wet leaves (big slip and trip hazard) couple bigger incline parts that you need to take at a good pace to keep going, the trail was also wet and muddy with some parts flooded making it a bit more difficult to navigate around and staying on trail, I got a foots soaker twice slipping off rocks and into the wet mud but the views were 100% worth it!! 12 view points all absolute spectacular

Views were amazing, but let’s just say you have to work for them. Really hard. Super mucky in spots, had to bushwhack around, especially with a dog, but overall super rewarding hike. About 4 hours so bring snackies :)

Always a great trail. Extremely muddy in spots, especially the descent from the last ridge, the trail is basically a swamp  in that particular area and you have to to do some bushwhacking, we benefited from prior knowledge and knew how to find dry passage yet rejoin the trail.  3:28 to complete
Amazing fall scenery. Excellent vistas. Muddy but manageable. Also saw 2 moose at Rutter lake

I went to Algonquin Provincial Park for my 22nd birthday with my two friends in July 2025. Unfortunately, I made the mistake of not taking into consideration that I am a beginner hiker. The park had beautiful views, but because I was in distress from the slopes, every view felt repetitive to me and I could not enjoy the park to its full potential. Throughout the hike, I would become excited at the sight of the hiking signs showing the distance we have walked, knowing that we were getting closer to being finished rather than being excited at the scenic viewpoints. Just to be noted; this was fully my fault. Although, I was mentally fighting demons on this hike, these pictures will never do it justice. Lesson learned: do not hike the Centennial Ridges Trail with zero hiking experience.

More like rain forest hike on October 6. Usually just the downhill forest section is muddy but with this much rain the entire trail was muddy and slippery (just the section on rocks surprisingly was something to look forward to that’s not mud and slipping hazard) I’ll give it proper 2-3 consecutive sunny days before going back on the trail for others who are booking their permits. We had our hiking shoes and would encourage a proper boot given how muddy most of the sections are.

I went in intending to do a short out and back to the first outlook, going counterclockwise. However, turned around sooner than that because it was raining heavily, and the muddy and slippery conditions were getting to me. Still, a beautiful walking the woods, I'll be able to challenging terrain. I will return on a dryer day.
Very muddy
Not bad at all for a difficult one
Very muddy....Ontario Provincial Parks should add some boardwalks and maintain the existing boardwalks to facilitate passing through the muddy areas by the river.
Wear good hiking shoes,
Beautiful weather, incredible view
Did this hike last year also. Spectacular views highly recommended trail. Good shoes are a must!.
Challenging but worth it. Many muddy sections. Many bare rock face scrambles, would be very difficult in wet conditions or without the proper footwear.

Lots of mud and tree roots, poles helpful for the steep sections. Spectacular views of the park from most of the ridge points. Appropriate clothes hung and shoes required (NOT jeans and trainers!) Come prepared and it's a gorgeous walk. Plenty of fall colours!!!
Every uphill track is rewarded with a beautiful scenic view
Great hike. Very busy.
Trail took a solid 4 hours to complete, very muddy/wet. Great views but colours aren't at peak yet (Sept 30th).

Amazing hike with varying terrains to navigate. The whole hike is chocked full of views - lakes, streams, beaver dams and many, amazing vistas. Must do if you have time and up to a difficult  level trail!
Great trail.  Definitely 4hrs... I didn't stop much.  Amazing views at many spots.  Lots of mucky spots too... my hiking pole helped me keep my balance.   Great hike.
Beautiful, best day hike in the park hands down. Not quite peak colors yet (sept 29th),but the viewpoint is amazing as always
Not quite peak season yet but we're getting there. Trails are really busy during fall so keep that in mind when it comes to parking. Expect some muddy areas on this trail (always)
A little muddy on parts but there are sections that are dry to get around it! Beautiful views, beautiful weather, and the leaves have started to change colour!

Quite muddy the day we were out! Wear hiking boots with traction and hiking poles would be helpful on steeper inclines and descends. We walked in reverse to stop 11 & 12. The views are worth the bit of sloshing up in mud.
Beautiful views. Not quite fall colours. Very muddy. Didn't have service at first but full trail about 10km. 3 hours at a good clip.
Muddy but still beautiful

Great hike today! Trail conditions are currently still very muddy - lots of careful navigation on rocks/roots/leaves to bypass mud and water, but totally doable with hiking boots.
Colour is starting but still early!
Good trail overall. Muddy at times, but other than that, it was well marked and a fun experience.
Fantastic trail with many scenic points. Rough terrain so prepare accordingly.  My GPS mapped it to be 10.36km.
This trail takes at least four hours. It’s not for beginners and is quite challenging. From the parking lot and around the loop is approx 11km. The trails are well marked. Enjoy the views. !

Pretty good conditions compared to what can happen around this time of the year in Algonquin (my 4th September here). Trail great as always, feels less daunting the more you do it. The leaves have started to turn!
Every uphill climb the reward, a great view

I hiked on September 11 2024...The trail was muddy in parts ...but I have good hiking shoes ,so I was fine and stayed dry.No bugs.. I think Post 4 and 5 of this trail have the best views of the Park..they are spectacular..well marked...I would give it a difficult rating, although I am 63...
It is a challenging hike with a lot of great terrain and views. Give yourself enough time if you would like to stop and sightsee.
beautiful and stunning views!

for sure one of the best day hikes i’ve been on in ontario. even on a windy cool day, the constant ups and downs keep you warm. you traverse through lakes, streams (literally walked up a couple small streams jumping  from rock to rock). the views of forest scapes and lakes are sprinkled throughout at the perfect times just when you’re legs are getting tired of climbing rocks.  

would not do this trek without proper footwear.  or at the least not when it has rained recently.

Super wet and muddy from all the recent rain,make sure to wear proper boots! It's very chilly along the bluffs this time of the year so make sure to dress warm but over all conditions were good. Some super wet areas but easy enough to traverse around
So beautiful, and peaceful early morning. Muddy and slippery so be careful, especially on the downhill sections, but very worth it.
A little muddy in spots but easy to get around. Great trail. A good level for us just starting out. Amazing views and good places to stop for a snack

Took 4.5 hrs for my husband and I together with our three dogs one of whom is blind - otherwise 3.5-4 is doable. Very muddy in some sections but overall a lots of fun and spectacular view on the ridge side
One of the best hikes we’ve ever been on, took it slow but gosh it was beautiful. Difficult at times, lots of different elevations and whole lot of mud!
My husband and I and our dog  Sophie we hiked the trail  today! It was so busy today on the trail lots of people! Some spots were very muddy so wear the right foot wear! Beautiful views like always!
Beautiful views, very fun trail with a lot of variety and viewpoints at different stages of the hik
Beautiful trail with some great views! It gets extremely muddy after a heavy rain, bring waterproof boots, you’ll need them!
It was muddy but the views were worth it!
Was quite muddy and lots of streams going down and across the trail due to heavy rains last night but wonderful views!

Exceptional views, but very steep so stay safe. Some numbered posts are hard to find (they’re wood and blend in) and you might miss them. Very muddy at certain points and lots of roots so make sure to wear good shoes. Definitely recommend even if it’s just for the view point!
Beautiful trail with nice views! But muddy but not too crowded mid week :)

The trail was muddy in some sections, but nothing terrible. There are some steep parts, but the views are well worth the effort. The guide at the start of the trail said that it would take at least 6 hours to complete. This is an overestimate, as it took us approximately 4.
Great trail and lovely views. Little muddy after the rain. Well marked and well travelled.

This is a spectacular hike that has some steep sections that bump it up to a moderate difficulty level. I am 67 and in fair shape and feel that rating is accurate for All- Trails. Due to recent rains a lot of the trail  was muddy and running with water. However, persevere and you will be rewarded with beautiful views from up on ridges of Algonquin Park lands. There are multiple ridge spots along the hike offering such vistas and great stopping points for your lunch or snack. Hikers are encouraged to walk clockwise on the hike. However, if you want a quicker way to the first high vista and are not inclined to do the entire loop go counter- clockwise. It is about a mile or so to a high viewpoint that way. This time of year we experienced no bugs on the hike but did have a couple of brief showers pass through.

The views are pretty much right at the beginning of this trail or on the last post. So if you want a shorter hike do it backwards to see the best view or only do the beginning 4 posts if you want a shorter hike. Over all great views. Was pretty muddy and wet because of storms the last few days.
Some wet spots but not too bad, some great views along the way and amazing view of the lake at the end
Moderate ++... more difficult than mizzy lake, but we were lucky because it wasn't muddy
One of my favorites, work up a sweat and see really beautiful scenery. Especially middle of October.
Trail is clean, well managed. Muddy areas. Steep inclines,  and great views
Quite challenging trail with plenty of ups and downs, great views on the top of the cliffs though!
Algonquin

It’s an alright trail, crowded at the end since people start from the end of the trail for the view. 

Track and tower or booth lake are better options if you wanna good view
Great views, make sure to bring lots of water and bug spray
Beautiful views from the top!  Some bugs and mud in spots but overall well worth the climb!
Great view,as always. We saw a large beaver at Cloud Lake.
She’s a long one! But so worth it for those amazing views!
Amazing trail and great views!
The views are amazing, and the terrain was varied.
Bring bug spray. No bears or moose sighted.

This trail is absolutely spectacular and my favourite day hike in Algonquin Park. It offers several beautiful cliff-top views of the surrounding area. Although the trail is more wooded than I would have preferred, the numerous cliff-edge viewpoints make it worthwhile, providing breathtaking, seemingly endless vistas. Definitely take your time and savour the views on this one.
Mosquitoes!!!!! So many of them and it made the hike terrible. Come prepared! If it rained think about not going. The views were beautiful tho!
Nice hike with decent views. Bugs are bad.  Not overly difficult but just weather related technical sections (navigating mud and water) along with tree roots.

Great hike, until it started raining hard. Wife saw a bear close to where the trail splits up. Was minding its own business but warning to everyone.

Stunning views, excellent hiking trail because of the variety

It can be very muddy in spots. Added a photo or two to indicate that. All muddy spots are very passable.
Beautiful challenging trail. Bring bug spray
Nice hike! Not too tough but lots of ups and downs. Moderate bugs, especially in the woods. Great views from the ridges.

We really enjoyed this trail! It was a relatively difficult trail, lots of varying terrain, you’ll definitely get a good sweat in, but the views were fantastic! We were one of the first on the trail in the morning, we went in, hoping to see some wildlife, but unfortunately did not see any other than some frogs. Lots of habitats that looks very suitable for a moose, but we did not see any. Regardless, the views are worth the hike. 

The trail is extremely well marked. Overall, a great trail. 

We did encounter some areas around the water that were pretty buggy with mosquitos, however- it could have been much much worse. Not too bad.

We had a full day of hiking in Algonquin Provincial Park, as we tackled the Centennial Ridges trail, a seven-mile loop with more than 1200 feet of elevation gain. The views from the top made every step worthwhile!
really nice rugged trail.  today there were very few bugs BUT it was quite muddy. hiking boots would be a great idea.
Hard trail but very rewarding

A moose extravaganza and an awesome trail!

Moose #1:  spotted alongside the main road during my 11 minute drive to the trailhead

Moose#3: At Cloud Lake - Just caught a fleeting glimpse as I startled it and it galloped and splooshed away. 

Moose#4:  Spotted on the other side of Rutter’s  Lake, near the end of the loop. 

The trail itself was fantastic- great views and nice walks past tranquil lakes and beaver ponds.  Yes, it was quite muddy but that’s to be expected in this lake of lakes and bogs
Quite muddy, but still accessible. Views are nice but not stunning.

This is a tough trail. The route has lots of slopes many with a lot water, mostly streams ( with the stream and the trail being one and the same). Come prepared with water and snacks. The vistas are spectacular!
Wet, but we’ll take this over hot and buggy any day!
The hike is easy and the views are good too
My husband and I and our dog sophie we hiked the trail  today! I ls a difficult trail in spots but amazing views!
Awesome hike. Views, lakes forest
We went in May after/during rain and the mosquitos were wild. Be prepared. Nice views overall and good in & out of woods.
Great roadtrip with Erika taking the RV for its first grand adventure!
Trail has lot of bugs and scenic lookut is good. Be prepared!
there were so many mosquitoes. highly recommend wearing a bug net
Muddy

I always say these are the best views in the west park on the second best trail. It's muddy on a dry day in places, but worth the rock hopping effort to get to some of the lookouts. It goes without saying, but please wear hiking shoes (not runners or flip flops) on this trail.

Very nice spring hike.  Mostly dry with a few bog/streams,  easily crossed without getting wet.  Bugs were generally non-existent except for a few black flys in wet areas.  Overall excellent  hike and conditions.
Stunning trail, quite wet as expected this time of year, boots are a must!
Trail was well marked. However, it was pretty muddy in spots so proper footwear is a must. Bugs were not terrible but bug spray or a net are recommended.

My husband and I hiked the trail  today! Unfortunately my phone  was acting up so it didn't record our whole hike  but the lookouts are beautiful! We loved seeing  the 3 moose! Very tough trail to hike in spots and very wet and muddy right now!
Rocks can get a little slippery when it rains. Awesome elevation changes that may be slightly difficult for some people. Spectacular views and well maintained trail make for a great hike.
Decent spring hike. Not too busy, and no bugs at this time of year. A little muddy but the trail is clear and easy to navigate.
Pretty muddy. Lots of up and down
Beautiful but very muddy due to rain - trail took a long time because of this
Plus 2 kilometers each way! Epic!

My favorite Algonquin hike. Lookouts were spectacular.  Some snow on the trail, but nothing significant. Still some hanging ice. Note the road to the parking at the trail head is closed until spring.  this adds 2KM each way to the hike! Still worth it
Trail not groomed at all very deep snow
Cliffs and scenic views

Trail up/down both ridges from the intersection are well travelled & packed down. The trail section between both main ridges is less travelled/packed. Careful foot placent is required. Gaiters could be helpful if less experienced.

Beautiful views but some fresh snow slowed us down today didn’t bring snowshoes. Was wearing crampons. Trail def has some elevation so not for beginners! Ooooo and one last thing I tried to get into the hike through Raccoon lake but someone with a plow plowed half of it and left so I couldn’t get my truck all the way up the driveway. So I hiked in from highway 60 and added the 4 plus km to the hike.
super muddy but very easy to navigate
Main entrance closed, park at raccoon lake. Slippery and muddy. Great views! Saw 2 moose.

Main trailhead is closed and currently under maintenance as of October 19th. We parked at Racoon lake as an alternative.

Trail has stunning views and a decent climb. Trail was slippery and muddy but to be expected as it was raining. Good trail markers! Took our group about 4 hours.
Strenuous and challenging.  Great trail great workout

Trail does take a while - about 3 hours, especially if you’re stopping to take pictures. Views are awesome! Can be repetitive but the lakes in the middle are beautiful and worth it. People below saying it’s muddy, which it is, but fine with proper shoes. It got busy at the end as people hike to one view and then turn around. Most people were walking straight through the mud instead of around the sides at one point. Go early to avoid the people there for the instagram pics and the people who don’t know what they’re doing.
Snow shoeing
My husband and I and my dog  Sophie we hiked the trail  today! It is a difficult trail on a dry day today it was slippery and muddy in lots of spots!
beautiful views!!

Great trail, lots of ups and downs, multiple lookouts, very well marked. I was there after the peak of fall colours...25% of trail was washed out or extremely muddy, trekking poles would have been helpful. Even with the mud I loved this trail and it was definitely challenging. I kept a quick pace other than when trying to get through the mud and barely stopped and it took 3 hours.
Very muddy
Favourite trail at Algonquin, the views are non comparable
Amazing views from the lookout points. Hiked on a rainy day so was extremely muddy and slippery. Def reco hiking shoes and poles!
Hiked in a gloomy and rainy day! Def super muddy. You will need a proper boots and poles. It was hailing a bit too
Heavy snow during hike, had to abort midway and return. Beautiful views at periodic intervals though.

looks good bit muddy
My new fave hike in Algonquin Park.  Only took 2.45hrs.  A fun trail - lots of lookouts.
Stupendous views of the forests and lakes. There are great markings for the trail.

Note that the trail is shorter than advertised - it goes to both parking lots, but you only need to go to the one where you parked.

The entire upper ridge, and even some of the lower ridge has view point after view point. If there is a crowd at one, move to the next - they are all great. 
This trail was less crowded than Track and Tower - probably because it's slightly off Highway 60 and longer. 

Take your time, breath the air and enjoy the views. If it's hot, slow down and rest - it's not an easy trail.

Trail had fantastic views (we went in the fall) during its busiest season the trail still didn't feel jam-packed. My group went through it very quickly but you can lead a very leisurely pace and still do it in under 4 hours.
Perfect conditions October 2

Great trail with some difficult spots but in general very manageable. We did not complete the entire path but stopped at one lookout because it was running late. Great view of fall color over the beautiful Algonquin Park. Highly recommended.
great view of fall colours

Gorgeous views
Pretty difficult with lots of ups and downs and roots and rocks. Great workout.
Impressed with my 7 and 10 year old for completing this with me!
Fantastic trail - moderate one and can be done in 4 hrs
Great hike with university gang.
Favorite trail at Algonquin.  Saw a beaver building a dam.  Amazing views.  Very crowded at the end, however.  Lots of people didn’t do the loop and only went straight to the views.
Pretty busy this time of year but absolutely beautiful.

Trail was nice and dry for a change! 
Fall colours were stunning.

Absolutely worth every step! Very well marked and the trail is easy to follow, although I'd perhaps avoid it if it's been raining as there are a lot of rocks and roots that could become slick. It's a good workout and if your knees or hips are problematic you may struggle with the ups and downs. The sign at the entrance says it takes an average of 6 hours to complete, which is probably waaaaayyyy off for safety sake. The sign had me concerned so I hightailed the first 7km and avoided doing the out and back to Racoon Lake campground... it ended up taking me 2h45min with a stop for lunch.
Will absolutely be doing this again!

Incredible trail! Multiple view points! If you follow the trial using the blue markers (not the white), the views just keep getting better better! Definitely on the more difficult side with many roots and rocks, and constant inclines and declines.
We actually ended up seeing 3 massive moose right by the parking lot as we were leaving! So incredible to see.
Great Trail. A lot of up and downs and a lot over rocks - the lookouts are fantastic, the colours are amazing. We saw a moose today, very impressiv.
Nice hike, interspersed segments of incline and decline. Multiple nice ridges as lookout points / lunch spots. Decent fall foliage for this time of year but likely even better in a few weeks!
Amazing trail, some mud but easily avoidable.  Lots of climbing over rocks and roots, but all doable for this early 60's couple.  Views are spectacular,  best of Algonquin.
Amazing views. Definitely my favorite trail in Algonquinn park. No bugs. Some mud spots but nothing to worry about

Well marked, lots of roots and rocks but no problem if you've got boots and watch your step. Sometimes I find trails rated as moderate are actually much easier, but this is definitely worthy of the name. Took me 2.5 hours solo with minimal breaks and good pace. Incredible views at the end of September and no bugs.

AMAZING

Great as always. Some muddy/slushy areas, not difficult to avoid.

Moderately challenging hike with rewarding views along the cliff edge facing west. Some mud and wet areas along trail but no bugs. Sign says it takes 6hrs to complete and app shows 3, but expect around 4hrs to complete this 10.6km trail hike. Leaves still mostly green on Sept 16.

Beautiful day hike in Algonquin Provincial Park. Alltrails rates it as moderate but as an avid hiker, I'd say it's closer to 'moderately challenging ' or hard. This is due to elevation gain and loss, rocks and roots and varied terrain. 
A few mosquitoes in the thickly forested areas but not bad at all. 
Really enjoyed the beaver dams. The elevated lookout views are incredible! I preferred the North East section up until Cloud Lake opposed to the South section.
Completed it in 4 hours including a couple of breaks and lots of photos.
Amazing views and varied scenery. A bit rough on the feet with lots of roots and rocks.
Beautiful views! I completed this trail in 3 hours with a few short breaks to look at the views. Definitely worth hiking.

Mostly dry with a few muddy spots. Not a lot of bugs, but quite a few other fellow hikers :) The trail is somewhat rugged with lots of branches and a few rocky slopes, so good footwear is recommended.
Nice lookouts, manageable muddy spots.
Trail is well marked and easy to follow, with a little attention to the blazes. Fall color starting to turn and leaves falling.  Beautiful vistas, lakes and beaver ponds.
Beautiful trail with amazing lookouts. I didn't do my research properly beforehand so I ran out of water. I would highly recommend this trail just bring lots of water and give yourself plenty of time

It’s long but not difficult. The initial ascend leads to a long walk on the ridge with beautiful view. Muddy and buggy in the wooded areas. Final lookout point is a view of the lake of two rivers. Spotted beavers hard at work and chipmunks stocking food.
Beautiful view, a bit muddy in some areas.
A great for a day hiking. Beautiful views.

Excellent. Completed it in 4 hrs with 45 mins for breaks. Lovely walk along boulders with fab views across the valleys. Highly recommend. If you want just the vista across Whitefish Lake (which I highly recommend) start at 13 B and do just the last portion and back. Probably more like 1.5 hrs.
Challenging and very muddy but worth all the effort. Make sure to take boots or waterproof shoes and carry water. We didn't see any wildlife except for an otter.
Amazing trail.  It was def 13k, not 10. Challenging but so rewarding.  Lots of amazing views.   Muddy in spots but not hard to navigate around.  Just do it!
Lovely trail. Beautiful views. Worth the effort
Great trail with varying terrain and fantastic lookout points. Only a few bugs for us and only a handful of muddy spots that can easily be avoided/crossed. Definitely worth it!
Muddy

Moderately difficult, very well marked and pretty busy trail, with lots of ups and downs. Make sure you wear decent shoes or boots, a lot of the trail is very wet and muddy. Surprisingly not many bugs which is great!  Lots of awesome viewpoints and things to see.

Adventurous hike! Still very muddy in many spots so be prepared to rock hop a lot. Saw a couple wearing sandals which I do not recommend. It’s a challenging and longish hike but superb views. I noticed a lot of interesting looking mushrooms.
Record is out and back to the first look out ridges.
A bit muddy but a great view and challenging adventure

A challenging but worth it hike. The views are amazing throughout the whole hike. If it’s been raining or wet make sure you wear waterproof hiking shoes, you will encounter very muddy and flooded out sections. Be prepared, take water and snacks, enjoy the views.
Amazing hike beautiful scenery and look outs specially point 10

We hiked this trail with 10 kids ages 5-15, took us 5 hours including our lunch break. Definitely had a lot of muddy shoes, but the kids loved getting through the muddy obstacles!! We were lucky to spot a moose at the start of the trail, and the lookouts and small lakes were lovely.
Muddy but great lookouts! Took us about 4 hours to complete.
My husband and I and my dog sophie we hiked the trail  today! It is a difficult trail we have hiked it now about 6 times now! Lookouts are beautiful!

This is an amazing trail. I would consider the trail itself to be medium in difficulty. The length makes this trail harder. Bring a lunch and snacks for sure. It's a must to visit this trail if you are staying in Algonquin Park.
Muddy spots, so watch your feet!

The trail is amazing, a super challenging hike for sure but super worth it. The washout in spots gets hairy and the markers are in odd spots so watch for that. But the bugs weren't bad and the trail wasn't super muddy. We hiked it after the massive storm they had up here on July 11th. Happy hiking. Leave no trace.

It was less humid because it hasn't rained for a few days, but there was plenty of bugs and muddy areas throughout the hike. All in all it was fantastic and the ridgelines are great viewpoints and breaks from the hike. Great exercise and a solid distance.
Beautiful views. A couple of muddy spots but nothing bad at all. I put on bug spray before hand and was largely left alone. I’m a pretty fast hiker and finished in about 2hrs45.
Muddy with lots bugs in the forested section. However, the view on the ridge was well worth it.

Not to many bugs during the middle of the day. I still wore pants and brought my jacket. I saw a Black Bear from the 1st set of cliffs. Lots and lots of hills :) 
2 hours 54 mins.

Beautiful day. You could see so far into the distance today over all the ridges. 

Bring water and a snack for lunch with a view. A bit muddy. Great hike.

Incredibly beautiful, my favourite trail in the park! The view of the last ridge is unbelievable, especially in the fall when the leaves change. Also it's a perfect length - the few hours makes it worth the drive in, but not too long where you're not sure if you can do it

Great trail.  Loved the views along the different ridges.  Mud in places necessitate proper hiking boots.  Mosquitoes are out big time so wear pants, long sleeves, and spray. Nice trail with some lovely views. Plenty of moderate up and down, wet and muddy in places but the views are worth it!
