Awesome trail

The trail was muddy in many areas but the fall colours were spectacular when you got up to the ridges. 
I disagree with a number of other reviewers who have said that this trail was a 'moderate' rating. The distance itself is not the problem. The elevation changes are pretty significant and the footing on the trail is difficult. You spend a good deal of your hike looking downward, because you are constantly stepping on, or over, tree roots and rocks. I would rate it as 'difficult' solely for this reason. I encourage people to do the hike but go prepared.
Amazing Trail full of up and downs. Not recommend for small dogs as it’s wet and not easy to climb up.
A bit wet and muddy, but less than I would have expected given the rainfall over the last week

Great views, dog friendly but lots of people. Around three hours to complete  including photo stops. Moderate due to multiple elevation changes and length. Definitely worth it! Hiked on 9/20/21 around noon.

Breathtaking views!  We stumbled upon a large beaver dam and many lodges.  Be prepared, it’s a moderate hike.  Lots of roots and inclines.  I was thankful to have my walking poles to keep my balance.  We left around 8am and completed it in 3 1/2 hours with plenty of time to take pictures and enjoy the views.  I would do this hike again!

Good trail, great views when you reach the top. Yes, there is a lot of uphill, but it's worth it to see the views, especially at the north end. However, if you do the whole loop, the last third, until you reach the end of the loop, is very, very rugged to the point of just wanting it to end.

Moderate hike, lot of elevation changes.  Heavily trafficked, no bugs with plenty of photo opportunities due to the many scenic overlooks. Our small beagle Cooper had no issues. Definitely worth the 3.5 hours.
Beautiful. This trail is no joke though. Come fit and prepared

The trail is very well marked for the most part, we got off track a couple of times but easily found our way back. Awesome trail. Certainly not for anyone who does not hike much but it was not difficult, just short ups and downs and lots of roots and rocks. Gorgeous views!!! I would do it again in a heartbeat!
Super nice! Moderate is appropriate because a bit long. But definitely not hard. Landscape is amazing. Took us 4 hours with a lot of pauses for photos and lunch. Recommended!!

Amazing trail. It's longer than it says it is. I started at 8am and finished 2pm. You need to give yourself at least a 6 hour window to see all the look outs which are amazing. You can only do this in 3 hours like some people have on here if you are not stopping and not looking at the lookouts. First trip ever to Algonquin and it was worth it. I did not find the trail to difficult but I am in good shape, I could see this being hard for people that are new to hiking so come prepared!

Algonquin Park's best trail. there are 5 or so lookouts on this trail from varying heights. I loved hiking it in the fall to see the colours. there are also small lakes and ponds, and a great lookout at the end overlooking White Fish Lake. 

the condition of the trail was fair but it's a decent amount of work and climbing. I'd say plan for 5 or 6 hours if you are planning to stop and enjoy the views.
Wonderful views! Totally worth it:)
Beauty trail, difficult for fat guy like me. Gorgeous look outs and challenging terrain. Definitely have to go back
This is a very difficult trail and definitely not 3 hours. It’s difficult and takes the average person around 6 hours to come. Gorgeous and really lovely. Just long and not moderate.
Big challenge, totally worth it!
A great hike
My favorite trail in Algonquin every uphill stretch your reward is a great scenic view.   It should be rated hard not moderate.  The trail is in great condition.

Not for beginners... challenging terrain with many elevation changes. Perfect for hikers looking for a rewarding trek. Incredible views!!! Worth the climb.  Total elevation of 553m according to my tracker. Lots of inclines and declines... not for those with knee issues unfortunately. 
Many stops along the way with a variety of scenery from meadows to little lakes. 
Bring lots of food and water and wear hiking boots. Challenging footing along the way. 
Trail markers visible for rhe most part with only a few spots that were challenging to follow.
Took us approximately 5 hours to complete. I would like to meet the people who completed it in 2 and shake their hands... they must have ran through this rugged terrain. 
Be prepared and have fun!! 100% worth it.
First time in the trail, very rugged.  Took us 4.5 hours with stops for photos. Bring water and your fitness.  Go early, plan your time. Worth the hike
Very rugged, with steep climbs. the views were spectacular. Took us just under 4 hours,  with a few short stops for water and pictures.  The best trail we've been on yet!
Beautiful trail. Climb is worth the views. Took 2.5 hours. One of the best trails in Algonquin.
Fantastic workout. It’s a good challenging hike with some incredible views.
Done in 4.5 hours with a small dog, photographers and a short lunch break. Worth the uphill for the views!

A great hike with a good mix of elevation, views and lakes (small and bigger). The trial is really well-marked and maintained. We finished it in 3hr 20min with lunch break abs a couple of water stops. After Labour Day the trail was not busy and there were no bugs! I’d love to do this hike again.

Great trail- well marked with plenty of lookouts that is easy to get to from Hwy 60. Some challenging climbs but the trail is very well marked. We got their early to avoid crowds and it was fairly quiet

This hike was beautiful! As a BC girl used to steep climbs, the elevation gain was not a problem and most of it was flat. What a beautiful welcome to Ontario for me. 

The trail was well marked and the views spectacular. Be careful along the cliffs, there’s nothing to keep you from the edge. Don’t forget to read the booklet at each post! We didnt realize until we were done the hike and it would have made it educational. 

All in all, lovely.
Amazing views, favourite hike in Algonquin

Best views can be had for less than 2 miles round trip if you go counter clockwise. the loop is nice but would be better when leaves are changing or already off the trees, so you can see all the lakes. watch the trail markers. it's very easy to go off trail because it's so rooty and rocky, you have your eyes on the ground a lot!

Awesome hike - beautiful views. Went out on a Friday morning at ~9am, occasionally crossed another set of people (total 6-7 groups) in the 3 1/2 hrs we were out there. Stopped to sit at once or twice and felt alone most of the hike. started the hike with about 5 cars in the lot & finished around 1pm with 30 cars.

Gréât five-hour hike (with two small dogs and a long lunch break) . Wear hiking shoes at a minimum. We went in September so no bugs and the weather was cool and dry. Could see how muddy it would get in wet weather. Mid-week at 9:00 is a good time to miss the crowds.
Awesome!! Beautiful views
Somewhat challenging. We got it done in 2 hrs and 45 minutes but we kept a decent pace with a 5 min break. The views are spectacular. My favourite trail to date

This trail will reward you with spectacular views!! While the park guide lists it as difficult, I would classify it as moderate and well worth the climb to the ridges. We were there yesterday & it took us 3.5 hours, with a few stops along the way to take in the views. Be sure to take lots of water and your camera. There are lots of tree roots on this trail, so a good pair of running shoes or a good hiking boot would be your best bet for footwear. Some mud and a few mosquitos along the trail. Overall my favorite hike to-date and you won't be disappointed with the breathtaking views. It will be the first one we do when we come back next year!

Amazing views, definitely a little challenging especially in today's 30+ heat. Bring lots of water! 
We managed to complete it in about 4 hours, that was taking small breaks to enjoy the view and a 20 minute stop to eat lunch.
There were some spots still muddy, but they were easy to walk around. Puppy loved it too, and enjoyed showing me where the pools of water were. Hehe

Centennial Ridges was a challenging trail, but so much fun! The views are amazing for the cliff tops! Quite rocky and lots of roots along the trail, make sure your wearing hiking boots or running shoes. This trail would be hard to do during or after it rains as it can get super slippery. All over, I would 100% do this trail again!

Lots of shade walking on pretty trails combined with many lookouts. Ridges are beautiful. Took us 4 hours. If you are a regular hiker, it's an easy/medium level hike. Overgrown in some small sections.

We did this with our 2 kids and a dog. Take lots of water if it's warm, no place for fresh drinking water for your dog. He probably drank close to a litre on his own plus what we needed. Elapsed time was 3:50 with breaks, total moving time was 3:12. Do not recommend wearing flip flops as we saw a couple people coming in wearing . Amazinf views, so many lookouts. Really a great hike. Not too muddy or buggy. It's hot right now, feeling like high 30s, so lots of water is my only suggestion.

Beautiful trail. Lots of steep inclines going up and down cliffs. Definitely not for the faint of heart but the lookouts were beautiful. Mosquitos weren’t bad at all. Worked out to be approx. 11.1 km. Trail is very well marked with lots of blue markers.

Beautiful views. The last lookout over Whitefish Lake would be a great out-and-back sunset viewing location (I plan to go back). Several red herring trails so pay close attention to markers and/or GPS.

Great trail. Lots of panoramic views - much better than the lookout trail. I was able to do 7 hikes in Algonquin and thought this was the best. Mud wasn’t bad and was able to finish in 2 hours with a distance of 10.2 km as measured by my Apple Watch in hiking mode. There is quite a bit of up and down so be prepared for a workout.
Perfect conditions! No bugs. Incredible views throughout trail. A new favourite :)
Minimal bugs, lots of mud but 1000% worth it ￼
A little muddy in some places but it was a really nice hike with some great views.
Beautiful lookouts but it’s difficult! We are in our 40s and fairly active and it took almost 6 hours. It’s really long but worth it.
Saw a moose!!!

Fairly challenging but worth it for the views.  if you're doing multiple trails in a day, I'd reccomend doing this one first. Not too muddy compared to some other trails but theres still some mud.  Completed in 2 hrs 20 mins with some stops to take pictures/videos.
was very muddy towards the end, but my girlfriend and I loved it!! recommended!
Did this trail for the first time, it did not disappoint. Incredible lookouts throughout! It was muddy in spots throughout the trail, but well worth it

Hard to beat in terms of scenery. My first time was 2019.  I have been back multiple times since.  It's one of a few trails worth going back to visit again and again.  If you go at a decent pace with brief rests to take in the view it is doable in less than 3 hours.
Nice hike with beautiful ridge lookouts, definitely recommend wearing boots, muddy in many areas.
Great trail! Loads of stunning lookouts and lakes. Was a bit muddy, but otherwise NO BUGS!!
Beautiful...mud! But a great hike with unmatched views
Great workout. It’s actually 12.5kms AllTrails seems to always have wrong distances. Very muddy but very few bugs surprisingly. Amazing views !!!!!
Beautiful views along the entire hike, there was always another section to look forward to! Overall great hike.

Good trail, lots of good lookouts at the start and end elevations, 4 climbs but the first one is the only one that is grindy, that said you do get quite a bit of time on a decline as well. At the points that are overlooking the cliffs it can be sunny and hot, inside the forest section the bugs and mud were pretty rough (mud particularly on the final stretch). Took 4 hours including some stops for food, trail towards the end of the loop is not marked as well as the rest, bring lots of water and enjoy.

Great trail with incredible views - cliffside, forest and lakes.

I'd rate it as hard, not moderate. Lots of elevation and fairly long - with elevation I clocked about 12km. Some stretches weren't marked very well so pay attention and don't be afraid to double back. Very difficult/uneven terrain much of the time - rocky, extremely muddy areas, a fair bit of scrambling. Watch your step!

Overall, a very tough but also very rewarding hike. 

**I will add that unfortunately I sprained my ankle midway so the second half was very tough in a bad way, hence the long finish time. That doesn't change my rating, though; just means I'm determined to return but be even more careful. :)

Great trail with a little bit of everything - forest, lake views, streams, lookout views. Moderate-challenging. Some areas were muddy but I was fine with balance and non-waterproof trail runners. Bug spray was enough to keep the bugs away.
A little muddy but great. Finished in 4 hours with water breaks and stopping for lunch.

spectacular views, beautiful water. This is a challenging trail. Be prepared to get a little bit muddy.  There are quite a few parts of the trail that you need to step onto logs or rocks because of all the mud. The
 trail took us 5.5 hours with breaks.  check the weather before you go as we ended up in finishing the trail in the rain.  loved every minute of it.
great fun trail with various kinds of views. Good exercise and wild blueberries. Bug spray is a must in mid-July after rain. Quite a lot of puddles as well.
muddy and buggy around cloud lake. awesome views!
Muddy but the view was worth it

Fabulous views and a must do. We biked the Algonquin Rail Trail to here and started at Coon Lake. Muddy at spots but there was heavy rain the day before. Well marked trail. Hardly any bugs. We did this in just over 4 hours with some stops for snacks and enjoying the views.
Very muddy in places but spectacular views.
It’s definitely a hardcore trail. Long and lots of ups and downs.
Great trail, poured rain most of the hike but kept the bugs away!
Not for beginners.
Wonderful trail!
So many ridges and vistas to lookout - beautiful well marked trail, some low lying muddy areas that were difficult to navigate through day after a very rainy day.

Great workout! Did this trail as a trial run for carrying my backpacking gear. Wouldn't recommend carrying 30+ lbs and doing it in the rain... although it's doable! No moose but beautiful views even on an overcast and rainy day!

Great hike with stunning ridge views and beautiful lakes along the way. A good moderate level hike with areas of steep incline, flat, and downhill portions. Completed in approx. 3hrs20mins with a few stops for photos and snacks along the way
Absolutely beautiful. My group just went to the lookout and it was not too difficult. The full trail would be worse but with enough time, easily doable.
amazing views, good gradients for fitness hike.  no bugs whatsoever! dry, no mud after yesterday's rain.  my teen boys loved it!

My favourite trail so far. A large portion of the trail is along the ridges - keep your dogs leashed! Gorgeous views. Well marked. Parts of the trail is rocky / has tree roots so make sure you have the right shoes.
Amazing views when you get to the top but be prepared for lots of mud and mosquitoes. It gets pretty intense in some parts when you’re going uphill but totally worth the view of the lake at the top!
Beautiful trail, showcases many different types of ecosystems that can be found in this amazing area. Lots of birds and beautiful sights. Bring lots of water and bug repellent!
Lots of bugs and some pretty intense cardio but SO worth it. Come prepared with lots of water, snacks, and bug spray.
My boyfriend and I and my dog  sophie we hiked the trail! Lots of beautiful spots for pictures! Be careful of all the roots and rocks  though!
Really nice single track with a little of over growth, but nothing really to complain about.  Many good lookouts by cliffs and ponds
Great...buggy

Gorgeous trail with lots of up and downs but totally worth it for the views on the cliff tops and overlooking the park & lakes!! Hiking boots/ankle support highly recommended. Bug spray/bug jacket also highly recommended!
good views from the top of the ridge overlooking the water at the end of the trail.
Beautiful scenery, but the mosquitoes were awful!!
Awesome full day hike. Lots of bugs and mosquitoes but brilliant views and terrain
Very scenic trail - loved the views. But you definitely need to have some kind of mosquito repellent!

Very nice lookouts, but full of mosquitos!!!

Preferably have a mosquito head net and wear a long sleeve shirt.
The views are good but anyone not fully covered can hardly enjoy them due to the mosquitoes
Difficult and lots of mosquitoes

Lots of mosquitos at this time of year, but the views make that annoyance worth it. Nice diverse trail with great lookout points along the way to keep it fun. Fairly easy hike overall. Would make for a fun trail run too.
Great trail, lots of rocks, incline and great views. Mosquito season has begun, bring spray/protection.

This trail was amazing! It's a loop trail that took us about 3.5 hrs to complete. It had lots of inclines/declines and different types of terrain. The views are absolutely stunning and make this trail a must try!
Beautiful trail. Very challenging
First hike of the year on this trail.   Excellent conditions for the most part. Some muddy areas that are easy to with go around or straight through.   Quiet on a May week day.
Challenging hills.

I love this trail! this is my second time doing this one and it never disappoints. it has a bit of everything. lots of cardio, but great stretches of nice walking as well. You also get the enjoyment of finding your way through the mud on logs and rocks. very fun trail! really awesome lookout views as well.
Beautiful trail ,great  views  and lookouts.

awesome trail… you got rocks, you got mud, you got obstacles… stunning panoramic views of algonquin, all paths clear, enjoy!!  it’s a bit challenging but if you’re looking for some good cardio, this is it!   this is no barkley marathon but it does the trick!

Amazing hike, beautiful hike full of different habitats!!! Longer than it says here, was 11.3 k in all without going up to Coon Lake, plan enough time you want to make sure you have enough light to get back! The many obstacles courses we had to go through to get past the mud made it more challenging but lots of fun for those who enjoy the challenge!

The trail was amazing, viewpoints are awesome. Lots of rocks and lots of mud so waterproof boots were essential. Trees are still naked, and the trail was empty, I didn’t see a person, still low season. It took me 3.5 hours.

Today the temperature was a bit colder -7C, very windy but sunny. Snow was perfect to walk on, as long as you follow the trail.Everything was hard frozen. I brought snowshoes and ski polls just in case, I never used either one of those. Very windy on all ridges and a bit icy, but no crampons needed. The distance from the Hwy 60 to the parking lot is about 30 min walk one way. Overall trail can be done in about 5-6 hrs depending on how the snow condition is.

March 13th. 
The access road (2km one way) is still snowed in, the snow is deep and soft due to the warm temperatures 
The trail is flooded 500 m from the trail head. You can try to cross using a fallen tree or just cross in the water ( like I did) just know that today the water was thigh high and it took me 3 big steps. 
The snow is soft and deep lots of sinking including on the ridges.
Some fallen trees and large branches on the trail.
High wind on the ridges 
if you are up for a challenge and a good workout this hike is for you 
Gorgeous views as always on this trail!

Definitely consider this as challenging hike in winter!! Went yesterday... felt like -20 outside but still gorgeous ! Absolutely no people in winter , was only our group and another 2x people!! Definitely recommend! Consider wearing winter pants
More challenging than it seems, especially with winter road closures and thick snow
Easy to find & follow, challenging route but beautiful view, get there early!

Trail was nice and can be tough at certain parts. Unfortunately could only make it 1/3 of the way as time was running out (didn’t want to get caught in dark) plus stepping in 2-3ft of snow each time sucked. Also the entrance is closed and it’s like a 2km hike just to get to the starting point. Lovely scenery and we’ll definitely come back to finish the rest of the trail.

Went yesterday after a fresh snowfall, it was also snowing throughout the day but my goodness it’s gorgeous. The road is closed to get it so it adds about another 4km. But still a beauty walk! The trail is on the tougher side with a lot of uphill, and honestly I would NOT feel comfortable having children on that trail - especially in winter. But absolutely gorgeous!!
Lots of snow, being proper footwear! Awesome trail, lots of great views.  Parking lot is closed so be prepared to walk an extra 2km each way. Well worth the extra km's.
Great trail.  Best views of all the HWY 60 hikes.

Went hiking here yesterday, the unplowed road and most of the trail being 1-2 feet deep of snow definitely requires some extra work.  We didn't do the full loop so we wouldn't get stuck out there past dark but even then we still did about 12k with the addition of hiking up the road!

Amazing trail. Lots of great views and various terrain. In Winter, extra 4km of unplowed road adds a bit more cardio. Very well marked, but it is a good idea to have a flashlight and the trail map to navigate confidently when dark.

I attempted to hike this trail today but the entrance to Centential Ridges road (off Highway 60) was chained off. The note there didn’t seem to indicate it would open any time soon. It’s a 2km walk to the trailhead from that point. I didn’t bother and did the Track and Tower trail instead

Such a scenic trail, it was quite difficult and a lot of up and downs but totally worth it for the spectacular views. I went in September and missed the colours changing. Will definitely be coming back to this trail in the fall. Keep an eye out for wildlife!
The best views are toward the end of the loop directly overlooking whitefish lake. Nov14: was muddy at times but usually avoidable. Was too late for the fall colours.
Absolutely beautiful trail and decent workout. I think I missed the best colours by a month, but that's just a great excuse to come back.
Difficult trail but the views are worth it. Easily spent 1.5hrs taking pictures. Start early to get back before sunset
What a beautiful, challenging trail. Experience will make this hike more enjoyable,  and the difficulty is in the sheer distance it covers. I would definitely redo!

A really fantastic trail with a great mix of areas, some tougher climbs, and lots of rocks. Hiked it on Nov 7, and found the trail in good shape, with a few muddy patches. Completed in 4 hours, including a stop for lunch. The final summit view (around the 9km mark) is worth every step.
Had a great hike. Very challenging, especially this time of year. pretty muddy but nothing impassable. awesome views and some great scenery throughout.

Beautiful hike. Lots of ups and downs, not for the weary, but definitely worth it. Tons of vantage points. Didnt see any wild life besides squirls/chipmunks/birds. Lots of people were complaining because of the mud but there was never a moment I was forced to step in deep muck. Theres either a walk around, rocks or logs to cross over. Water proof shoes recommended, and ankle boots for stability, but not as muddy as I imagined based on some previous reviews - still muddy spots but not the whole thing. Took us 6 hours including stops but I'm very pokey. Took pictures at every stop. Stopped for a couple longer breaks for snacks and just to relax. Definitely could have picked up the paced and completed the trip in a shorter amount of time. Also someone mentioned a few days ago there was a fallen tree that was blocking he parking lot - they removed it yesturday so you can get right to the parking lot. Also - the visitor centre said access to the parking lot would be not avalible in 2 more days however because the weather is nice they are keeping it open longer than planned - so for the foreseeable future if weather continues like this.
Tree fell before the entrance so there was a bit of a walk to the trail's actual starting point (no access to the parking lot).
Great hike.  Alot of up and down hiking. Weather was cool so wet areas were frozen.
Muddy, very muddy

Perfect length and difficulty for a great hike. Views are amazing. At least half the time you will be hiking on wet or muddy trail which will be no issue with ankle high waterproof boots. I hiked on October 23 2020. It took me 5 hours because I stopped to take lots of photos.
Strenuous when wet:’) would highly recommend waterproof trail hiking shoes. Great scenic points throughout though, would highly recommend!

Excellent hike! The climb was worth the views and the vistas! 
We started approximately at 11:00pm. Took us about 5-5.5 hours to finish the entire loop. 

Stopped along the way to admire the beauty and  took a whole lot of pictures. Most of the leaves have shed but the yellow maple is beautiful. 

Route taken: 
We started at point 1 and did it clockwise to point 12. We saved the best views for the last. The panoramic view at the end is worth the steep climb.  

Tips:
1. Parts of the trail are muddy because of the rain. So be careful. 
2. Some rocks are pretty steep so be mindful of your step. 

One of the best fall hikes ever!!
hard trek. very mucky at this time of the year. amazing views.

Incredible!!!! We started late (3:30pm) and didn’t get out until 7:30pm. We had to hike down from lookout 11/12 in the dark and I don’t recommend that without really good shoes and a flashlight. However, the entire hike was phenomenal. Lookouts galore, diversity in the forest, trails that are interesting with lakes and waterfalls. Ahhhh! Just go! 

Tips: wear good, waterproof hiking boots. It’s muddy and wet on many of the trails, rocky and root-filled in other parts, and you’ll do some climbs on rock slabs. 

Recommend going the direction they suggest with the arrow at the first Y-intersection (blue trail markers) — especially if you are night hiking at the end. 

The guides say leave six hours but we are pretty experienced and did it in 4 hours total, stopping for tons of photos and drone footage, and eating on the go, plus ending in the night hike. So, don’t be dissuaded if you are experienced from doing this with not a lot of time left in the day.

Trail markers are reflective which is a huge bonus for night hikes!

Have fun!!!
Really beautiful views over the ridges. Very muddy though!
Beautiful views. Very muddy
Lots of up and down inclines. I would definitely recommend this trail if your up for a challenging adventure ;)
Tough but rewarding. Can't believe we did it in 4 hours!
Great views.  Muddy in early Oct.  Approx 10km, took 4hrs at a steady and good clip.  Good workout.  when entering the loop take the loop clockwise to save the best view for last.
Quite muddy so I hope anyone who attempts the hike has good waterproof footwear !! But overall a great hike; many different landscapes from marsh to breathtaking cliffs. Will do this hike again.
Muddy
Lots of beautiful lookouts, very muddy after a heavy rainfall the night before but still manageable! Great hike
mucky in a loft of spots
Beautiful lookouts
Amazing views, but extremely muddy which made a challenge

If you have to choose 1 Algonquin trail, don't listen to the ratings and do Track and Tower instead. More lookouts on this one, and certainly more challenging, but much less interesting in multiple respects. 2km of wow, then 6km of meh, then 2 more km of wow (and/or mud). Only reason I gave it 4 instead of 3 was because I saw a moose near the beginning which was super cool, and the lookout near the end was actually worthy.

Intermediate difficulty. Lovely colours. Make sure to arrive early during the peak fall season, the parking lot gets full in no time. 

The trail is a nice one, not too difficult. Lot of vantage points mean you will stop by for more photos.
Took a few hours with a couple breaks. Well worth it. Really wish people would follow the numerical flow of the trail. Would help with congestion.
Very muddy but good. Got really busy upon my return at 11.45. Parking was packed.

The autumn colours are just past their peak although still breathtaking. I started the trail late, just before 4:00pm and sunset was a few minutes before 7:00pm. I probably could’ve finished the loop before dark but that would’ve been to fast to really appreciate how beautiful it is. It did by sheer serendipity allow me to arrive at the cliffs above Whitefish lake facing west just as the sun was setting. Amazing sight. That did mean that the last 1.5-2km was done in the dark. I had brought a very bright bike light so it was slower but doable. It would’ve been a lot less fun if I were trying to follow the trail markets without the bright light. There were zero mosquitoes or other biting bugs, which I understand can be fierce earlier in the season. It had rained the night before and so the trail was very muddy in places, even more challenging to avoid in the dark.

A stunning trail with fall colours on full display!  Many, many vantage points with fabulous views.  
We parked at the south end near the Coon Lake access point, not at the very busy parking lot to the west of the trail.  The Coon Lake parking spot only has room for 4-5 cars so be prepared for that if you arrive later.
I would rate the trail as moderate.  There are a few mucky sections as well as lots of rocks and roots to be wary of.  No real difficult climbs and definitely no sections where climbing or ropes are required.  The sign at the trail head states it is a six-hour hike.  We mapped the route from the Coon Lake access point to be about 11.5 kms.  We did it in about 4h 45m and we stopped an awful lot to take in the scenic vistas.  It can be done in under 4h easily if you wanted to...but take your time anyway as the views are resplendent!

Very picturesque trail with many viewpoints. Entire trail was covered with fallen maple leaves. Would rate difficulty as moderate. It is muddy in some sections but worth every step. I guess it will get too muddy if it rains.
Do arrive early since parking gets full very quickly especially during Fall season. We arrived around 10am on Monday and were lucky to get the last spot. People who arrived late did park on the road. Not sure if its permitted. 
It took us around 4 hours to complete this loop with all the stops to take pictures and have a quick lunch.

I would have loved this hike for only ONE of these views and I would rave about it for years but it was dozens of stunning views that take your breath away. Absolutely gorgeous, moderately difficult for experienced hikers, I would assume this would be very hard for novices... But worth it nonetheless. Bring a lunch, snacks and water and enjoy the challenge. Muddy in many parts so make sure you wear proper hiking shoes or at least ones with deep ridges on the bottom so you won't slip too much. Very few hikes in Ontario can even compare to this one in terms of beauty.

If you're coming on a Saturday in fall, arrive very early to get a spot in the lot. We parked at 7.15 easily (3 cars in the lot), came back to idiocy. Double parking in the main lot and cars parked roadside near enough all the way back to the highway which made exiting very difficult. If people are parking roadside - take a hint and park up at the end and do not drive any further.

The trail itself, as always, is amazing and even more so in fall. A little muddy in spots so bring suitable footwear. A lot of people hiking backward to get to the whitefish lake overlook first (thinking they're smart); the ones on the far ridge are far more beautiful and all you're doing is causing congestion on the trail. 

Still 5 stars but geez, people need to use common sense.

It was quite an experience considered its difficulty. However, as soon as you reached every single high point with enormous fall foliage view, your hard effort will all paid back. We arrived at the peak of this year's fall foliage and I would say we are lucky as there were no big rain nor strong winds for almost a full week before we arrived. The scene viewed at the high points will make you speechless. Proper hiking footwear is highly recommended as there were uneven rocky paths. Occasionally you will come across muddy sections. Bring enough fluid and energy bars for short breaks. My wife and I both spent over 4.5 hours to complete this trail with 3 mini breaks in between and several photo shooting breaks. A power bank would be handy if you will use your phone as your main photo shooting equipment. Overall it was an unforgettable experience. Will try on another trail next year!!
Fabulous fall colours, parking is crowded.

Good hike 
Very long 
Lots of ups and downs 
Don’t know if I would do it again 
Maybe just go see lookout next time

Long and beautiful! Was muddy and slippery in sections, but the lookouts were absolutely worth it. Definitely moderate in great weather, but would be tough in wet conditions because of mud and large smooth rock faces. Bring lots of water and snacks and arrive early! We arrived on a Saturday at 9am and had to park up the road.
Beautiful and can only expect better in the coming weeks.
awesome montain view
Absolutely gorgeous!! Best hike out here. Wouldn’t say hard but advanced. So many stunning views at every turn. Bring snacks!
Pretty muddy for a part .  View is good.
Very beautiful view and challenging road which is very fun but it is a little bit to muddy, either than that, the trail was perfect.
Beautiful trail! It poured rain on me a couple km in but loved it nonetheless. The views are incredible!

Easy to see why this hike is so popular. Amazing views and a challenging, interesting trail. I would definitely recommend hiking boots. I didn’t take mine but poles would be recommended, in particular for the descents. My small dog had a great time. My recording got messed up for some reason (user error). Finished in 4.5 hrs with breaks.

Very nice trail. Did it in around 2.5 hrs, with very minimal breaks at the vistas to take in the view. Very muddy at times, so I'd be careful to go after rain. Definitely wear hiking boots and pants. While it's not a necessity, poles would be useful for anyone with mobility issues, etc. And I'm not a trail runner but can see how this would be a good trail for that.
Little muddy but fun trail overall
Stunning.
This tail has the best veiw in Algonquin Park. It was vey wet and muddy in areas today.
This trail was great! We did it in August on a warm day so it was dry. It took just under 3 hours with time to look at the top.
The end is the best, perhaps do the trail backwards. Also it’s much longer than 3.5 hrs, unless you’re going to hustle.
Nice hike, but not really challenging if you hike regularly! Really nice view 1.5 km before the end!
Great views. However it’s very muddy so be careful
Beautiful as always.
It was the best trail ever and the view was amazing and the trail was so fun!

Like the reviewers below me, we got caught by Algonquins unpredictable weather and were hiking in the rain. We were prepared for rain, but not the level of mud there was! I slipped twice in the slippery mud. Some parts of the trail also turned into streams due to the rain which were difficult to navigate.
The views were beautiful and I would love to do this trail when it’s dry!

We were caught off guard by the weather and ended up hiking the majority of this trail in the pouring rain! The wooded sections of trail are very muddy but the views are worth it! Please ensure you hike this trail with caution as we came across one individual who broke their ankle and another who broke their knee in the last km of the hike. I believe both had to be carried out by paramedics/parks rescue team. Hope they’re both ok! Last km back to the parking lot was almost completely washed out...

Amazing views! It rained while we were hiking and by the end the trail was EXTREMELY muddy. Pack a lunch to eat while sitting at one of the lookouts. Lots of mud in the low areas,  but worth it for the views.

If dry, not too hard of a trail, squarely moderate. Though the day we went it was super muddy and parts of it flooded, making it very slow going. Parking wasn’t too bad, went Labor Day weekend, arrived at 11am, still had spaces on the shoulder.

A beautiful and rewarding hike, definitely worth doing. I would say this is overall a moderate hike with some challenging elevation and footwork. I didn’t find it that difficult but definitely make sure you have the proper footwear (hiking boots). It’s also a good idea to pack some snacks and enough water because if you do the whole trail (close to 10 km) you’ll be needing it!
Challenging hike with multiple impressive vistas, and visits to a few small lakes.
Trail was muddy in many locations. Views were good.

Our favourite trail on the Highway 60 corridor - we do it every visit! In total takes about 5-6 hours with a couple breaks, recommend stopping for food around Post 4 as it has some nice views and will put you at a good pace for the rest of the trail. 

Some of the most beautiful views in the park, and varied too. Outlooks are gorgeous at the beginning, middle, and end, but there are also some beautiful lakes throughout. There are water sources if you're looking to pump your own water, but only in the middle of the hike. 

We've had a couple incidents with ground bees in the late summer and fall, so beware. Usually off trail thanks to the dog, but the one time when we found them on the trail, there was a warning sign put up by park rangers promptly
Fantastic trail. Lots of climbing and fancy footwork along the way. Lookouts are awe inspiring.

We hiked in the rain on 29/08, but it was so worth the beautiful misty views. For a seasoned hiker, I’d rate the trail as moderate. The rain however made navigation quite tricky. Lots of up and down and uneven ground but so worth the view.

This hike was so amazing. I would say if your a regular hikwr then  this would be intermediate but of your not then this one is on the hard side. multiple changes in elevation and uneven ground combined with wet conditions. scenery from the multiple cliffs is breathtaking. I see someone reviewed as just ok I completely disagree.

Nice trip on this circuit, second time this year. Most notable difference: fewer bugs. In early July, it was nearly unbearable. Much nicer this time around. Always nice on the final ridge, with the magnificent view of the lake and island.

We saw some nice ducks
Would rate it moderate instead of harder,amazing look out points. Definitely recommend going going in the morning (less busy)

Kick butt trail!!  ups, downs, roots, mud, and
 rocks.  This is a real hike, not for the weak at heart.  Our 8 and 10 year old did great, my knees not so much.

Great trail with plenty of elevation changes (very little flat) and wonderful views of Algonquin park. I would rate as moderate, as others have mentioned, and doesn’t take 6 hours. Not that 6 hours isn’t doable on this beautiful trail, but that would require a LOT more stopping, snacking, picture taking and sunbathing. We hiked after a day of heavy rain and the trail wasn’t as muddy as I expected at all. The bugs weren’t out in force either (always a good thing!) I searched high and low for a sighting of my first moose, but alas, I left disappointed. Just another reason to return to this trail and gorgeous park!

Amazing views within the first few km's from the ridges. A challenging hike but 100% worth it. Lots of steep hills and rocks , took us around 5 hours, definitely give yourself at least that much time to fully enjoy it. We were fortunate enough to see a mom and baby moose amongst the pines within the first couple of km's! The best views are near the end!!! This has been favourite hike in the park.
Rugged terrain with amazing views.

Hike was okay. Some spots with great views, but most of the hike isn’t amazing. We did see lots of wildlife though, including some moose which was great! Would definitely classify this as a moderate hike rather than a difficult one. Conditions were pretty good. Muddy in some places but not many bugs around.

Amazing vistas on the bluffs. Elevation changes are easy with no real switchbacks to speak of. Overall a safe and moderately challenging hike for beginners; experienced hikers will find it easy. Heavy rains would make some sections trickier than others.

We hiked on Aug 13 and the trail was very dry, with only a couple minor muddy spots. Bugs weren't a big issue.

One of the harder trails at Algonquin, but if fit, definitely would consider this moderate instead of difficult. Moderate elevation gain for views of the forest from above. Some moderate uphill/downhill sections after you hit the first spot. Lots of rocks/roots and rock face traversing on the ridges. Small lake along the way, with the option of checking out Coon Lake if you have time. The final lookout/ridge area is the most worthwhile, with a lovely view of Whitefish Lake. Bet it would be an amazing sunset spot. If you wanna hit this area first instead of doing the majority of the trail beforehand/at all, just hike it in reverse. After the view of Whitefish Lake, it's about 2km back to the parking lot. Finished in 2.75 hours.

Loved this hike! It took my husband and I 4 hours to complete (Aug 9), we stopped for a total of 1 hour for lunch/enjoying the views. I would rate this hike more moderate than difficult. Once you're over the climb in the beginning, the hike isn't too bad to walk. Be careful after post 4, there is a wasp nest on the ground, run through it if you can.

The views this trail offers is amazing!

Great hike with excellent views. Went yesterday (August 8) and conditions were near perfect - no bugs, only a couple muddy patches which were easy to move around. Agree with rating of difficult - would be just moderate for fit and springy hikers but more challenging for the casual hiker with the technical footing and elevation changes. Highly recommend this hike!

Enjoyed the hike.  Lots of elevation changes to panoramic views of the park.  Post 7 was the unofficial lunch spot for many.  Heard about large bees nest early in the hike and fellow hiker was stung.   Moderately traveled even for a Saturday during the summer.  Definitely will consider hiking again in the fall.
Great trail with awesome views
Rainy day beautiful

Fairly straight forward trail once the initial climb is out the way. Great views and as others have said, definitely one for fall. The section up to the final ridge climb is a bit of a slog on hot days, especially if buggy after rain.
Great hike. A little wet and buggy after the rain but the views are worth it.  I would rate this as moderate not difficult
Great hike. Beautiful views in the fall.
A great hike in Algonquin, trail is well marked the entire way.
Awesome

I love this hike !!
Challenging in certain areas but nice views
Amazing views. Took just under four hours.
Lots of ups and downs, but was a beautiful day. Took about 4 hours because we decided to take pit stops.
Bring extra bugspray, Nick's lookout is the best view.

Great trail! Took us 4 hours with lots of stops to take photos of the spectacular scenery.  The view of the cliffs at cloud lake is one of the nicest spots.  Lots of exposed roots and rocks - wear good shoes!
Amazing views

It was great!! 
Please take more water bottles and mosquito spray.
lots of shade, took us 4 hours with plenty of breaks. no bugs, spectacular views. highly worth it.
was able to do the trail in 3.5 hrs even with us not being hikers

Phenomenal trail--a must for the area. Lakes and rock cliffs and varied terrain...what a treat. If it weren't for the DEER FLIES (mosquitos not bad), I wouldn't have whipped through the trail so fast (3hrs) and would've loved to stop and take it all in. My long pants/shirt + scarf-around-ears with ball cap proved to to be way to hot and effectively attracted more bugs I'm guessing...

Beautiful views, challenging but not too hard. Definitely worth going if visiting Algonquin. It took us 4 hours with a lunch break and a few water breaks. Did not find the bugs bad at all. After reading the other reviews I was worried, but there were minimal.

we decided to take this trail on the first day of our vacation in Algonquin Park in 2018. I ended up fracturing my ankle at the 4k ish mark... let's just say this trail was hard before I fractured my ankle.  it was quite difficult and felt alot longer than 10km
however, amazing views!

Beautiful beautiful!! Was as tough as expected. Lots of ups and downs. Challenging, but rewarding with spectacular views for 2 moderate hikers. Took us about 4 1/2hours to complete with frequent breaks. Plenty of bugs this time of year. BUG SPRAY is a must
This trail is amazing! one of the best hikes ive done! The scenery from the different cliffs are excellent! It took me 3 hours at a good pace with maybe 30minutes of that to stop and take pictures.
Injured my ankle the day before... still made decent time
An excellent challenge for hikers of various levels. Plenty of ups and downs. Views from the ridges are excellent. Bring bug spray ... they were nasty in places.

It was our first 10k hiking experience and we were travelling with 4 people and a dog. It took us about 4.5 hours, but we had some big breaks. It definitely has a lot of great views!! Saw a few snakes, but they were harmless. Got sidetracked once, but this app helped us get back on track! We hiked it yesterday and we barely saw any people at all. At Every lookout point we were the only people, which is incredible for this trail!! I would not do it again since it was a little bit hard, but definitely something you should do once for sure!

Magnificent  Took me 3hr15min with my dog. Took two short breaks. Stunning views. Very clearly marked. I used bug spray and I think I came out with only one bite. So worthwhile. Wasn't busy. Sunday, July 5th.

Great hike! with beautiful views worth the climb up. 
As can be expected there are lots of rocks as this is canadian shield and bugs  are bad this time of year. 
i would rate this trail as moderate not difficult.

Path is way too rocky. Feet hurt a lot halfway into the hike despite having good hiking shoes. Also the real view comes almost at the end of the trail at the 10km mark. Most of the trail up until that point is mediocre at best. Also there were A LOT of mosquitoes and flies throughout the trail (June). Effort to value ratio isn’t that good but if you’ve already done booths rock and have time to kill then this is good.
It’s a 10k trail with stunning scenic views and lots of lookouts!
Nice trail! Including a few breaks, it took us just under 3:30 hrs. My Garmin watch clocked it at like ~10.25 km.

What an experience! Me and my friend started the trail around 10am and finished at 2pm. We took a few breaks during the way to enjoy the amazing views. I would highly suggest doing the full trail as you will get to see a lot of different scenery. You can also go down by the water after finishing the trail for a swim!

Bugs were not that bad and didn’t see a lot of snakes. Overall, great experience!!
Beautiful trail with amazing views!

My favourite trail so far. Lots of hikers and I haven’t seen any snakes. The view at the top is breathtaking! Just pay attention to the markings you will easily get lost. enjoy this trail!! Enjoy the view!! A must hike trail in Algonquin Park!!!

A decent hike, not overly difficult. Followed the trail markers and went clockwise, which was definitely the right choice. The views while along the ridge are beautiful! The forest sections are mediocre in comparison to other hikes in Algonquin. The trail needs some grooming. We began around 8 am, and didn't see anyone else until the beginning of the trail. Parking lot was almost full when we got back to our car. Took us around 3.5 hours with two 10-15 minute breaks. Saw a black bear between marker 8 and 9! As with all of Algonquin Park, expect bugs.

So many amazing view points! Never stops! Decent workout if you like crushing hikes!! 

Funny story: we got attacked by a large bird! Very scary! But I think it was protecting its youngly! I’m sure it won’t be there by the time the next hikers come along! (Attacked when we were 8/10km deep)
it's quite difficult. I would say it's hard.
Very beautiful and challenging trail. Highly Recommended
Long trail, lots of bugs, lots of incline but worth it. Will definitely back in fall season!
Great trail really good day hike that is abit challenging can be done in 3 hours but take your time and enjoy it., go clockwise and take water, enjoy the great views.

We did this trail back in November, a little late on the review. The trial could be challenging depending on if it is still muddy. Make sure to pay attention to the trail markers, you could miss it at some places. Overall a great trial! Definitely recommend it!

This is a workout, especially if it is one of multiple hikes in one day. We completed this after hemlock bluff earlier in the day and felt it in the knees. Lots of elevation changes, but wonderful views, especially at the end. When I say end, I mean about 45 mins from the end. Since the trail hasn't been maintained because of the pandemic, you have to follow the blazes very closely, otherwise it's easy to lose it.

Did this trail in May, first weekend of the park being open after covid-19 closures. Very good trail, nice workout with beautiful views along the ridges. Do the trail clockwise and follow the blue signs (as suggested) so the best view comes last.
I can imagine this trail being very crowded in high season, even today there were a couple of groups being loud and disturbing the peace and quiet.
Go clockwise to save the best view for last.
Winter hike. Snowy and ice conditions.
loved every minute of this trail I highly recommend it
I did this trail on Friday Oct. 25th and saw only a few other people. It was really lovely! Some beautiful views and a decent challenge.

This is an incredible trail, we almost didn’t do it and so glad we did! Took our time and stopped along the way, 4 hours total. Would rate as easy-moderate. Not too tired after. Suggest doing the loop backwards for the most spectacular view early in the morning- wish we had. 
Monday, not too busy felt like we had it mostly to ourselves just saw a couple people. 10.30-14.30. Enjoy!

Nice views but if you’re serious about wildlife watching and enjoying nature then steer clear of this trail. There is so many tourist types walking and yelling at all times that you feel like you’re in a public mall not on a nature hike
Fantastic views.  But feels like being in the mall with all the people.

Went Saturday Oct 5 2019 with 2 kids, 6 and 9. Although the trail is long and lots of up and downs, it is not difficult to walk. Lots of great lookouts and it was the perfect weekend to see the fall colours. Lots of people on the trail though. We got there at 9:15 and the parking lot was full. We were the 2nd car to park at the entrance of the parking lot.  When we finished around 3:30 pm, the cars were parked 2 km away from the parking lot along the road! Definitely get there early during peak season.
Loved this trail!  It's a must if you are in the area.

anyone up for doing this trail this Saturday? (5th October)
if yes, email me: manhar @ gmail

Did this trail yesterday, it took me 3 hours with minimal breaks at the top of the ridges. I would rate the trail more easy-moderate, especially if you have experience. There are lots of rocks and exposed roots so I would recommend wearing hiking boots. Make sure to get there nice and early - returned to the parking lot at 11am and it was packed.

Gorgeous trail and quite challenging in some sections.  Be cautious of a wasps hive hanging just above the trail between 3 and 4 markers.  Many people were swarmed and stung.  
The fall colours were at their peak and the views were breathtaking.

Did this trail on September 29th 2019. Some steep sections, but definitely worth doing. You pass by a few amazing lookouts and 2 beaver ponds with dams. If you’re going to do 1 trail at Algonquin I highly recommend this one. It took us 3.5 hours at a fair pace with minimal stopping.
Absolutely beautiful!! Not a difficult trail.

We have done many trails in Algonquin and this is hands down the best one. We stopped and did photos and lunch and the trail took us 4 hours 15 minutes (30 minutes not moving), we also passed many people. Time wise I would not expect to do this in under 3 hours unless you were moving and only had a quick break. Plan for 4 if you are fit but want to stop and enjoy the lookouts.
Incredible views! Be sure to allocate for lots of break time just to take in the incredible scenery

What a great trail if you want to be rewarded with scenery all along the way.....trail is rated as hard but I think because of some of the rocky sections (not difficult).  There are plenty of view points from high ridge to lake views.  Definitely could be finished in under 3hrs with stops for views and lunch.

Gorgeous views. First lap last August 2 hr 30 min. 2nd lap yesterday with my son and 7 year old nephew. 2 hr 50 min. 3 rd lap today just me and my son 1hr. 44 min. definitely feeling 
that one. can't wait to come back next year.

This trail is brilliant.  There are LOTS of people on the trail.  This may have had something to do with the long weekend, but the trail is also rated as the park's best in a number of guides, so it gets a lot of attention.  It's worth it.  The views of the park are amongst the best, and the hike itself is a lot of fun.  Park says it'll take 6.5 hours, I was able to complete it in 4.  That includes a few breaks for food, and a couple of moments completely awestruck at the views I was seeing.  
Very early in the hike, you have a choice of going left or right.  The park has an arrow pointing left, and that's the direction I went.  If you go left, you'll hike most of the amazing trail before you get to the absolute best view.  If you go right, it's only about a km away.  I suspect there are guides out there that tell readers to go right.  The amount of foot traffic in the last two km's was significantly more than the traffic we saw in the first 8.
A couple notes on getting here.  The road is narrow, and gravel about 90% of the way there.  Don't drive in the middle of the road as the bends/twists can hide an oncoming vehicle.  I arrived about 10am and the parking lot was half full.  By the time I left, the lot was full, all driveways leading to it were lined with cars, and the road had cars parked at the side about 200m up the road.   It's busy.  Get there early.
Don’t bother reading the reviews/look at the pictures just believe in the rating and enjoy!

Up and down. Think of it like climbing up one step, walking a ledge and then climbing up to the next step. Same view from both steps. Signs say 6 hours, we did it moderately quickly at 3 hours and 20 minutes stopping for a couple of quick steps. Trail has segments that are tree roots and rocks, so your ankles will get a work out. Beautiful views around most corners. I’ve hiked harder “hard” trails... I’d consider this more a moderate hike then hard. It will push you tho.

Most beautiful trail I have ever been on. It is a long and treacherous hike but worth it for even the least expected hiker for those amazing views. Spent the whole day on the trail brought lunch and ate on one of the cliff side. Recommend taking your time and enjoying the scenery.

Absolutely beautiful views.  
Difficult trail - all roots and stones and climbing and descending.  Worth the effort though.

This was a nice trail. Super buggy though. Will honestly say that this trail shouldn’t be labeled hard, it’s more moderate. I did this with my family in 3 hours with a couple breaks. It’s a nice challenge with great views.
Wow! Make sure you pack bug spray and lots of water. It took us 5 hrs with a dog and lots of breaks to enjoy the spectacular views.
Great view, great variation, not that difficult, just short ups and downs! Excellent trail!
Fantastic mix of nature and beautiful lookouts. Exhausting yes, but worth it.

Probably the best 'official' day hike in APP - note that the actual distance is 10km - I doubled it for a challenging afternoon.

The views are great and with a total of ~450/900m of elevation gain your legs are in for a treat :)

For reference, I trail ran the first lap in ~1:20:00 (with a fair bit of walking whenever I otherwise may have stopped) and then hiked the second lap in ~2:00:00 with a ~10-20:00 minute break in between. Almost ended up biting off more than I could chew.
solid trail, lots of short steep climbs. great views I just wish there was 1 east lookout. all views faced west.
Beautiful!  I plan to return many times.  Easily done in 3.5 hrs of you are in shape.

Amazing landscape, a lot  wild blueberries,  this trail is HARDCORE  ever, up and down , bring enough water and some snacks and also bug spray. Me and
My husbands complete the trail I can’t believe. So  and the I don’t feel my legs anymore I took 2 aspirin for sleep
great  condition  for  outdoor  workout  the  best part about this  trail is the  view of  every  stop  totally  love it ❤

Moderately challenging trail with some nice lookouts.
It took us under 4 hours to complete.

July 27, 2019 - I really enjoyed this trail. Mix of lookouts and pretty forest. I stopped a lot to eat the wild blueberries along the ridges :) There’s a couple beaver ponds as well, one where you walk beside the ancient looking dam and see the pond above you. For me in late July there were hardly any bugs, tho it was also a windy day. Trail maps are available at the trail head, and trail is well marked.

This has to be one of the most breathtaking trails I've ever hiked. What an absolutely beautiful set of views around the park. I will definitely do that hike again in my lifetime. Took my brother, niece and I just over 3 and 1/2 hours to complete. If you didn't stop to enjoy the scenery it could be done in 3hr.
Brilliant trail with great lookouts! Only a few bugs were around
Very good trail. Muddy parts. Good views from the ridges. Super buggy in early July. Well worth. 3,5h to finish. Saw a moose on the way.

I did this trail today (July 1, 2019) with my partner and dog. It's a great moderate - challenging hike, with some steady inclines and beautiful views over Algonquin Park. Today the conditions were muddy at times and VERY buggy, and it's getting a tad overgrown at a couple of sections. The signage says it takes 6 hours but it took us 3.5 (athletes could do it in 3, I imagine)

Great hike! Labelled as difficult, I would say it is moderate to difficult depending on fitness level. Took a little under 3.5hrs to complete, including a few stops to reapply bug spray and enjoy the scenery. 
Great for dogs as long as they have good recall, or are kept on leash, especially on the ridge. 
Saw a moose just outside of the trail on the road!

I ran the trail last Saturday (22 June). it was quite busy but still OK, especially for European standards. 
trail was good, A LOT of bugs, especially at the lakes (of course)
I would have found the trail a bit boring to hike but loved the last part with gorgeous views down to the lake. 
Great for trail running. Did it in somewhat under 2 hrs with lots of photo stops (turtles, dragonflys, views)

Really nice hike, challenging, with gorgeous views. Finished in about 4-5 hours having stopped several times to take in the scenery. Lots of bugs in certain areas and at least some bugs throughout - but not as bad as I thought.

This hike was awesome! Very dog friendly our dog loved it. We had bug spray for our dog and for us and used it a lot, kept the bugs off of us so they weren’t a problem. So many lookouts and amazing spots for pictures. It says it takes people 6 hours but my boyfriend and I were able to finish it in 3 and half hours with our dog. Shade during the hike makes it really nice. A little muddy in some spots but you can get around it if you look for another way. We started around 10am and there was only one other person on the trail when we finished around 2 it was busier! Would definitely recommend this hike and make sure you bring water and snacks!!

We hiked the trail on a cold rainy Saturday. There was hardly anyone on the trail. Trail passes along ridges, woods and lakes offering great views. There were few muddy patches towards the end of the trail, hopefully things will get better in coming weeks. I would recommend the trail for anyone looking for a challenging hike with views!

This is the best trail in the whole park, but it's not for the faint of heart. Still quite muddy from the thaw, but the hike through the many tranquil streams and mossy forests are quite worth it. With four or five lookouts, this trail truly has everything. Hike time was about 4 hours with a leisurely pace and a stop for lunch. Happy Trails!!

Wow. The views from this trail are absolutely incredible. It was quite muddy and wet throughout but still passable. Lots of moose poop around but we didn't spot much wildlife. 

The winter gate was up so it added an extra 2km to get to the trail head. It was a tough hike but so enjoyable!

Incredible trail, though this early in the season you need to hike and extra 2km and out since the access road is closed.

The views were phenomenal, from high ridges to highland beaver ponds to giant glacial boulders to old hemlock groves.

this trail is so beautiful. I would say the only real challenge is the length of it. I took this trail May 5th and they had the winter gate up still. so that's an extra 2 km to the trail head. would love to come here again!

This hike is challenging but well worth the effort! The views do not disappoint. Always assume you will have to climb one more hill. I have hiked this trail in the summer and fall. I recommend you experience both seasons. Bring lots of water and light snacks.
great views, lots if elevation. took about 5 hours
This is the hike that I compare all others to...difficult but several summit views of glorious lakes and fields and forests! Bring lots of water and snacks...will take several hours to complete!

This one works you!  I did this solo on the first snow fall of the season in late October making for some very slippery sections.  I did it in about 4 hours but it took everything out of me.  In my opinion it has the best views in the park,  so totally worth the effort.
Did the trail in the snow and it was a beautiful trail! Definitely one of the harder ones I've done so far. I would recommend this trail to anybody who is able to finish the whole 10km loop.
Awesome hike at the end of fall season!
This was my first time on this trail. I can’t wait to come back! It was beautiful! Challenging with the hills but well worth it!
hiked this trail October 15 2018.   very challenging.  felt like more than 10km.  next time I will track with a GPS.
felt like more than 10km.   good challenge

Took 3.5 hours with a few food stops. Trail was not too hard, a little wet in areas (it rained the day before). The blue trail markers sometimes are hard to follow so we had to back track 2 times. The views were nice, mostly mountain top and lakes. I recommend arriving early to get a good parking spot, and wearing good hiking shoes.
The view when you reach to the top is breathtaking. Must have a good shoes. Definitely coming back next fall early in the morning when sunrise strikes

Went today and the colors were fantastic... Went clockwise and the views were nicer on the east side as there are more trees and no lake.
Took us about 4h but we had plenty of little stops. Would say hike is moderate as there is not a lot elevation gain.
Gorgeous views. A bit challenging but totally worth it. Took about 3 hours with minimum stops just to enjoy the view.

I do enjoy this trail. However I find it a little boring in sections. About 4 hours at moderate speed. Lovely vistas about 1/2 way. 
Good footwear is an absolute must in this trail as the rocks can be slippery. Do take plenty of water as well!
Know your limitations on this one as it can be lengthy.

Great trail for a day hike with beautiful scenery. 
must have: good hiking boots, comfortable backpack, plenty of water and food. My hiking boots were good but not THAT good, near the end of the 10km my feet were a little tender.
I definitely recommend this trail as a Medium in difficulty.

This trail has beautiful look out spots. 
The terrain is extremely difficult, lots of long, steep inclines. Bring lots of water and snacks. It took us a little over 4 hours to complete with few stops.

Awesome trail. I went with my parents (64years old) and it took us 6 hours to complete. The trail was slippy because of dramatic rainfall and we did stop and rest a lot. 
My mom regretted the trail, I would do it again. Lovely views, it had all I wished for!
Amazing and beautiful views.  The trail is well marked.  It will be a challenging hike for some as you must go up and down hills.  It's rewarding and would love to do it again in the fall.
was a great hike. really quick you come to a height you have a nice view. walk next to the edge for a bit so you can enjoy the view ;).

This trail is very beautiful as other reviews have noted! Great views from above which make for some lovely spots for a snack or photo. 80% of the trail is in the forest and this shaded, which makes for a very enjoyable hike on a sunny day :) 

Some inclines/declines are slightly steep - hiking shoes are certainly recommended. Not sure why this is rated as hard, although perhaps this is the case for out of shape hikers. Enjoy!!! ;)
Great hike, make sure to bring lots of water if done in the hotter months. Amazing views from the ridges. Would recommend doing the hike in the fall during the color change.
Awesome trail!  So many beautiful viewpoints while hiking along the top of the ridges! Technical hike which makes it interesting and fun!
Bring enough water! Took 5 hours carrying an infant

Super fun hike! I would consider it hard for only people who don’t hike often but if you like to hike a lot it’s more moderate then hard! If you don’t want to do the whole hike and just want to see the ridges do the hike backwards, you get to the lookout a lot faster (about 15mins) then going all the way around
Did the hike in 3 hours on a beautiful sunny day. Trail is well marked and well maintained. Nice views from the ridges. Needed definitely the bug spray in all areas except on exposed ridges.

Excellent look out stops, beautiful scenery for sure! Definitely whipped my legs into shape going up those hills. A bit buggy but honestly in June any trail is going to be buggy. It would be great for fall colours I'm sure!

Amazing trail. Likely the best marked hike south of Sault Ste Marie in Ontario. Lots of up and down for some very doable challenge with gorgeous ridge views, interesting lakes, and a variety of rock of forest. Trail in good condition with some muddy sections but not a real problem. highly recommended!

This trail is incredible. Definitely more difficult than regional trails like Track and Tower, but offers plenty of spots for views and rest breaks, if needed. I would also advise that hiking this trail should be done during weekdays in fall, for optimal fall foliage and fewer hikers. It is definitely a great hike to do with friends, and will help keep you in shape.

Holy crap!  If you wanna get in shape real quick do this trail a couple times!  Great hike, fantastic views, a little muddy in spots. Make use of those streams, especially during the final quarter and dip your hands and cool your head. The billboard at the beginning of the trail says 6 hours, I did it in just over 4.5.  Bring lots of water, bug dope, and snacks for energy. Hiking 101.  When you reach the sign after tying the loop, you get a sudden burst of energy. Harness it! Keep a cold beer in a cooler in your vehicle and enjoy it when you return.  It’ll be the best dam drink you ever had!

Loved this trail. Because of the climbs, a little more challenging than some of the other trails I've done in Algonquin. Have been waiting all winter for access to this trail to open up again so I can do it again:) great views.

Great, demanding trail.  Many muddy sections of the trail taken over by creeks.
Still worth the effort.
great Algonquin trail and well-marked!
One of my favourite Ontario trails!

Have done this trail many times. It’s my favourite trail closest to Toronto! Hiked it yesterday, road is closed during the winter so add 2km each way to your hike. The sign at the trailhead says the trail is 10km but every time I have done it my devices have shown around 13km. In the snow yesterday it was about 16.5 km and took us 6 hours. Winter hiking is not my thing, but the trail is still fantastic! Highly recommend!
Finished the loop with 5 hours. Beautiful view made the whole hiking full of exciting. Very wet and uneven surface, rain boots or waterproof boots could be more helpful.
First half is best. Turn back at stop 5 for a good 2 hour hike. Took 4 hours to do the whole thing
We finished the trail in 4 hours including stopping for pictures and breaks. The view is stunning.

Took 4 hours to complete the loop from car park - including breaks along the way. The ridges are beautiful and can be seen throughout the trail. There are various types of terrain, wet and uneven surfaces which makes this hike more challenging but it's not difficult. Proper footwear (trail running shoes or hiking boots) helps a lot.

The best trail on the highway 60 corridor in Algonquin Park in my opinion. :-) Beautiful vantage points overlooking the park. This is probably my favourite trail in southern Ontario since you actually do a fair bit of climbing which makes it more interesting. There is a lot of up and down so over the course of the entire trail, that adds up to fairly significant total elevation which is pretty unique for the area. Our dog also has a blast on this trail. We started calling her 'spider dog' because she obviously loves scaling the rocks so much. I wish we lived closer to this trail so we could do it more often.

Moderate to difficult hike. Took my husband and I 4 hours to complete. We went at a moderate pace but stopped a decent amount of times for long periods to take pictures and enjoy the views. We went the day after it rained so it was extremely muddy which I found made it more difficult. Lots of ups and downs but the views are well worth it!! the best views are towards the end of the loop.
Absolutely outstanding views!! Well worth it!
Great trail.  Hiked it with my daughter about 9 years ago.

I did this trail in the fall when the colours were at their peak. The views from all the look out points were amazing. By far the best day hiking trail in Algonquin but not an easy one. Be sure to bring plenty of water and some food.
This is the best day hike you can get in Algonquin Park. The views are amazing. Take some water and snacks. The trail is not easy.
Great trail. Lots of great views.But super windy on the top of the ridges

Awesome hike with lots of excellent viewpoints and plenty of terrain variety from bogs to blue lakes to rocky Canadian shield elevated ridges with breathtaking lookout points. We are in our thirties and were able to finish the 10 Km loop in 3 hours including rest and stops at viewpoints (mind you we kept a quick pace and heard that it took 4 hours plus for some others). There are some challenging ascents but it is worth it for the views. This hike will give you a taste of all that Algonquin Park has to offer, enjoy!
not an easy trail, but a great one. one of my favorite in the park
Incredible trail with many lookouts.  Definitely not an easy one though!
